translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 270
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 270

sentences.zh: 【後梁紀五】起強圉赤奮若七月，盡屠維單閼九月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: (Later Liang Records 5) From the seventh month of the year qiangyu chifenruo, through the ninth month of the year tufu danchan, in all slightly more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang Records 5: from the seventh month of 920 through the ninth month of 922, a period of slightly more than two years.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚戌，蜀主以桑弘志為西北面第一招討，王宗宏為東北面第二招討。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day gengxu, the ruler of Shu appointed Sang Hongzhi as the first commander for pacification on the northwest front and Wang Zonghong as the second commander for pacification on the northeast front.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the gengxu day of the seventh month, the Shu ruler appointed Sang Hongzhi first commander for pacification on the northwest front and Wang Zonghong second commander on the northeast front.

sentences.zh: 己未，以兼中書令王宗侃為東北面都招討，武信節度使劉知俊為西北面都招討。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, he made Wang Zongkan, who also held the post of Director of the Secretariat, overall commander for pacification on the northeast front, and Liu Zhijun, military governor of Wuxin, overall commander for pacification on the northwest front.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, he named Wang Zongkan, who also served as Director of the Secretariat, overall commander on the northeast front, and Liu Zhijun, military governor of Wuxin, overall commander on the northwest front.

sentences.zh: 晉王以李嗣源、閻寶兵少，未足以敵契丹，辛未，更命李存審將兵益之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin, considering that Li Siyuan and Yan Bao had too few troops and were not sufficient to oppose the Khitan, on the day xinwei again ordered Li Cunshen to lead troops to reinforce them.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Li Siyuan and Yan Bao too weak to stand against the Khitan, the Prince of Jin on xinwei sent Li Cunshen with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 蜀飛龍使唐文扆居中用事，張格附之，與司徒、判樞密院事毛文錫爭權。

translations.literal: In Shu, the Flying Dragon Commissioner Tang Wenyi held power at court; Zhang Ge attached himself to him and struggled for authority with the Minister of Works and Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Mao Wensi.
translations.idiomatic: At the Shu court, Flying Dragon Commissioner Tang Wenyi held the reins of power. Zhang Ge backed him and vied for influence with Mao Wensi, Minister of Works and administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 文錫將以女適左僕射兼中書侍郎、同平章事庾傳素之子，會親族於樞密院用樂，不先表聞，蜀主聞樂聲，怪之，文扆從而譖之。

translations.literal: Wensi was about to marry his daughter to the son of Yu Chunsu, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs. He gathered his kin at the Bureau of Military Affairs and had music performed without first submitting a memorial to inform the ruler. When the ruler of Shu heard the music, he found it strange, and Wenyi took the opportunity to slander Wensi.
translations.idiomatic: Wensi planned to marry his daughter to the son of Yu Chunsu, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Co-Director of the Secretariat. He entertained relatives at the Bureau of Military Affairs with music without first informing the throne. When the Shu ruler heard it, he was puzzled, and Wenyi seized the chance to denounce him.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚寅，貶文錫茂州司馬，其子司封員外郎詢流維州，籍沒其家；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day gengyin, Wensi was demoted to military adjutant of Maozhou; his son Xun, an outer-office member of the Ministry of Rites, was banished to Weizhou, and their household property was confiscated;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengyin, Wensi was demoted to military adjutant of Maozhou; his son Xun, an outer-office member of the Ministry of Rites, was exiled to Weizhou, and their property was confiscated;

sentences.zh: 貶文錫弟翰林學士文晏為榮經尉；

translations.literal: Wensi's younger brother Wenyuan, a Hanlin Academician, was demoted to magistrate of Rongjing;
translations.idiomatic: Wensi's brother Wenyuan, a Hanlin Academician, was demoted to magistrate of Rongjing;

sentences.zh: 傳素罷為工部尚書。

translations.literal: Chunsu was removed from office and made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Chunsu was dismissed as Co-Director and appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士承旨庾凝績權判內樞密院事。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academician Expositor Yu Ningji was appointed to administer the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs on a provisional basis.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Expositor Yu Ningji was given provisional charge of the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 凝積，傳素之再從弟也。

translations.literal: Ningji was Chunsu's second cousin once removed.
translations.idiomatic: Ningji was Chunsu's second cousin once removed.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，清海、建武節度使劉巖即皇帝位於番禺，國號大越，大赦，改元乾亨。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Liu Yan, military governor of Qinghai and Jianwu, assumed the imperial throne at Panyu. His state was named Great Yue. He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Qianheng.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Liu Yan, military governor of Qinghai and Jianwu, took the throne at Panyu as emperor of Great Yue, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Qianheng.

sentences.zh: 以梁使趙光裔為兵部尚書，節度副使楊洞潛為兵部侍郎，節度判官李殷衡為禮部侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: He appointed the Liang envoy Zhao Guangyi Minister of War, the deputy military governor Yang Dongqian Vice Minister of War, and the military governor's aide Li Yinheng Vice Minister of Rites, all as Co-Directors of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He made the Liang envoy Zhao Guangyi Minister of War, deputy military governor Yang Dongqian Vice Minister of War, and staff officer Li Yinheng Vice Minister of Rites, all Co-Directors of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 建三廟，追尊祖安仁曰太祖文皇帝，父謙曰代祖聖武皇帝，兄隱曰烈宗襄皇帝。

translations.literal: He built three ancestral temples and posthumously honored his grandfather Anren as Emperor Wen, the Founding Ancestor; his father Qian as Emperor Shengwu, the Substitute Ancestor; and his elder brother Yin as Emperor Xiang, the Lieh Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: He erected three ancestral temples and posthumously ennobled his grandfather Anren as Emperor Wen, Founding Ancestor; his father Qian as Emperor Shengwu, Substitute Ancestor; and his elder brother Yin as Emperor Xiang, Lieh Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 以廣州為興王府。

translations.literal: He made Guangzhou the capital prefecture of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He designated Guangzhou as the capital of his realm.

sentences.zh: 契丹圍幽州且二百日，城中危困。

translations.literal: The Khitan had besieged Youzhou for nearly two hundred days, and the city was in grave peril.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had besieged Youzhou for nearly two hundred days, and the city was in desperate straits.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源、閻寶、李存審步騎七萬會於易州，存審曰：「虜眾吾寡，虜多騎，吾多步，若平原相遇，虜以萬騎蹂吾陳，吾無遺類矣。」

translations.literal: Li Siyuan, Yan Bao, and Li Cunshen assembled seventy thousand infantry and cavalry at Yizhou. Cunshen said, "The barbarians are many and we are few; they have mostly cavalry and we mostly infantry. If we meet on open ground, the barbarians will crush our formation with ten thousand horsemen, and none of us will survive."
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan, Yan Bao, and Li Cunshen mustered seventy thousand foot and horse at Yizhou. Cunshen said, "The enemy outnumbers us, and they are mostly cavalry while we are mostly infantry. On open ground they could overrun our line with ten thousand horsemen, and not one of us would be left alive.

sentences.zh: 嗣源曰：「虜無輜重，吾行必載糧食自隨，若平原相遇，虜抄吾糧，吾不戰自潰矣。

translations.literal: Siyuan said, "The barbarians have no baggage train, and we must carry our own provisions as we march. If we meet on open ground and they raid our grain, we will collapse without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan replied, "They travel light, but we must carry our own grain. On open ground they could cut our supplies and we would fall apart without a fight.

sentences.zh: 不若自山中潛行趣幽州，與城中合勢，若中道遇虜，則據險拒之。」

translations.literal: It would be better to steal through the mountains toward Youzhou and join forces with the city. If we encounter the barbarians along the way, we can hold defensible ground and block them."
translations.idiomatic: Better to slip through the mountains toward Youzhou and combine with the garrison. If we meet them on the way, we can hold the high ground and fight them there."

sentences.zh: 甲午，自易州北行，庚子，逾大房嶺，循澗而東。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu they marched north from Yizhou; on the day gengzi they crossed Mount Dafang and followed the stream eastward.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu they marched north from Yizhou; on gengzi they crossed Mount Dafang and followed the stream east.

sentences.zh: 嗣源與養子從珂將三千騎為前鋒，距幽州六十里，與契丹遇。

translations.literal: Siyuan and his adopted son Congke led three thousand horsemen as the vanguard. Sixty li from Youzhou they encountered the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan and his adopted son Congke led three thousand horsemen as vanguard. Sixty li from Youzhou they ran into the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 契丹驚卻，晉兵翼而隨之。

translations.literal: The Khitan recoiled in alarm, and the Jin troops flanked them in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan fell back in alarm, and the Jin troops pressed them on both flanks.

sentences.zh: 契丹行山上，晉兵行澗下，每至谷口，契丹輒邀之，嗣源父子力戰，乃得進。

translations.literal: The Khitan marched along the heights while the Jin troops marched in the ravine below. Each time they reached a valley mouth the Khitan would intercept them; only after Siyuan and his son fought fiercely were they able to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan kept to the heights while the Jin force moved along the ravine below. At every pass the Khitan tried to block them, and only after father and son fought their way through could the column move on.

sentences.zh: 至山口，契丹以萬餘騎遮其前，將士失色。

translations.literal: When they reached the mountain pass, more than ten thousand Khitan horsemen barred their front, and the officers and soldiers turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: At the pass more than ten thousand Khitan horsemen blocked their path, and the officers and men lost color.

sentences.zh: 嗣源以百餘騎先進，免冑揚鞭，胡語謂契丹曰：「汝無故犯我疆場，晉王命我將百萬眾直抵西樓，滅汝種族！」

translations.literal: Siyuan advanced first with a little over a hundred horsemen, removed his helmet, raised his whip, and shouted to the Khitan in their language, "You have invaded our borders without cause. The Prince of Jin has ordered me to lead a million men straight to Xilou and wipe out your race!"
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan rode forward with a little over a hundred men, bareheaded and whip raised, and shouted to the Khitan in their tongue: "You invaded our borders without cause. The Prince of Jin has sent me with a million men to strike straight at Xilou and destroy your people!

sentences.zh: 因躍馬奮□，三入其陳，斬契丹酋長一人。

translations.literal: Then he spurred his horse forward, brandished his spear, charged three times into their formation, and beheaded one Khitan chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: He then spurred his horse, spear in hand, and three times charged their line, killing a Khitan chieftain.

sentences.zh: 後軍齊進，契丹兵卻，晉兵始得出。

translations.literal: The rear troops advanced together, the Khitan fell back, and the Jin army was at last able to break out.
translations.idiomatic: The rear echelon pressed forward, the Khitan gave way, and the Jin force at last broke through.

sentences.zh: 李存審命步兵伐木為鹿角，人持一枝，止則成寨。

translations.literal: Li Cunshen ordered the infantry to cut trees into chevaux-de-frise; each man carried one branch, and whenever they halted a camp was formed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunshen had the infantry cut branches into chevaux-de-frise; each man carried one, and wherever they halted a fortified camp sprang up.

sentences.zh: 契丹騎環寨而過，寨中發萬弩射之，流矢蔽日，契丹人馬死傷塞路。

translations.literal: Khitan cavalry circled the camps as they passed; from within the camps ten thousand crossbows were loosed at them. Arrows blotted out the sun, and Khitan men and horses fell dead and wounded, blocking the road.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan horsemen rode around the camps, and from inside ten thousand crossbows opened fire. Arrows darkened the sky; Khitan men and horses fell in heaps and choked the road.

sentences.zh: 將至幽州，契丹列陳待之。

translations.literal: As they were about to reach Youzhou, the Khitan drew up in battle formation to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Near Youzhou the Khitan formed battle lines to meet them.

sentences.zh: 存審命步兵陳於其後，戒勿動，先令羸兵曳柴然草而進，煙塵蔽天，契丹莫測其多少。

translations.literal: Cunshen ordered the infantry to form up behind them and warned them not to move. He first sent weak troops dragging brush and burning grass as they advanced; smoke and dust filled the sky, and the Khitan could not tell how many they were.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen placed the infantry in the rear and ordered them to hold still. He sent weaker troops ahead dragging brush and setting grass afire; smoke blotted out the sky, and the Khitan could not gauge their numbers.

sentences.zh: 因鼓噪合戰，存審乃趣後陳起乘之，契丹大敗，席捲其眾自北山去，委棄車帳鎧仗羊馬滿野，晉兵追之，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: Then, with drums and shouts, they joined battle. Cunshen urged the rear formation to rise and strike; the Khitan were routed and swept their forces away over the northern hills, abandoning carts, tents, armor, weapons, sheep, and horses that covered the fields. The Jin troops pursued them and captured or killed them by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Drums and shouts signaled the attack, and Cunshen ordered the rear ranks forward. The Khitan were routed and swept north over the hills, leaving carts, tents, armor, weapons, sheep, and horses strewn across the plain. The Jin force pursued them, taking or killing tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，嗣源等入幽州，周德威見之，握手流涕。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Siyuan and the others entered Youzhou. When Zhou Dewei saw them, he grasped their hands and wept.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Siyuan and his command entered Youzhou. Zhou Dewei met them, took their hands, and wept.

sentences.zh: 契丹以盧文進為幽州留後，其後又以為盧龍節度使，文進常居平州，帥奚騎歲入北邊，殺掠吏民。

translations.literal: The Khitan appointed Lu Wenjin acting governor of Youzhou, and later made him military governor of Lulong. Wenjin usually resided at Pingzhou and each year led Xi cavalry into the northern frontier, killing and plundering officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan made Lu Wenjin acting governor of Youzhou and later military governor of Lulong. Wenjin usually stayed at Pingzhou and each year led Xi horsemen on raids into the northern borderlands, killing officials and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 晉人自瓦橋運糧輸薊城，雖以兵援之，不免抄掠。

translations.literal: The Jin people transported grain from Waqiao to supply Jicheng. Even though troops escorted the convoys, they could not avoid being raided.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin hauled grain from Waqiao to supply Jicheng. Even with armed escorts, the convoys were still prey to raiders.

sentences.zh: 契丹每入寇，則文進帥漢卒為鄉導，盧龍巡屬諸州為之殘弊。

translations.literal: Whenever the Khitan invaded, Wenjin would lead Han troops as guides, and the prefectures under Lulong's jurisdiction were ravaged on their account.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Khitan raided, Wenjin guided them with Han troops, and the prefectures under Lulong were laid waste.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩自滑州入朝，朝議以河朔失守責之。

translations.literal: Liu Yan came to court from Huazhou, and court opinion held him responsible for the loss of the Hebei region.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan came to court from Huazhou, and the court blamed him for the loss of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 九月，落鄩平章事，左遷亳州團練使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yan was stripped of his rank as Co-Director and demoted to regimental commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yan was removed as Co-Director and demoted to regimental commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己亥，加吳越王鏐天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day jihai, Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, was promoted to Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on jihai of the tenth month, Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, was made Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 晉王還晉陽。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 王連歲出征，凡軍府政事一委監軍使張承業，承業勸課農桑，畜積金谷，收市兵馬，征租行法不寬貴戚，由是軍城肅清，饋餉不乏。

translations.literal: The prince had campaigned year after year and entrusted all military-government affairs to the army supervisor Zhang Chengye. Chengye encouraged agriculture and sericulture, accumulated gold and grain, purchased horses and weapons, and collected taxes and enforced the law without leniency toward the nobility. Because of this the military city was orderly and supplies never ran short.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning year after year, the prince left all military administration to army supervisor Zhang Chengye. Chengye promoted farming and sericulture, stockpiled gold and grain, bought horses and arms, and enforced tax law without favor to the great families. The garrison city stayed disciplined and supplies never failed.

sentences.zh: 王或時須錢蒱博及給賜伶人，而承業靳之，錢不可得。

translations.literal: At times the prince needed money for gambling and for gifts to entertainers, but Chengye was tight-fisted and the money could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince wanted money for gambling or to reward entertainers, Chengye refused, and he could not get it.

sentences.zh: 王乃置酒錢庫，令其子繼岌為承業舞，承業以寶帶及幣馬贈之。

translations.literal: The prince then set out wine in the treasury and had his son Jiji dance for Chengye. Chengye gave Jiji a jeweled belt and silks and a horse in return.
translations.idiomatic: The prince held a banquet in the treasury and had his son Jiji dance for Chengye, who rewarded the boy with a jeweled belt, silks, and a horse.

sentences.zh: 王指錢積呼繼岌小名謂承業曰：「和哥乏錢，七哥宜以錢一積與之，帶馬未為厚也。」

translations.literal: The prince pointed at the piled money, called Jiji by his childhood name, and said to Chengye, "Hege is short of money. Seventh Brother ought to give him one pile of cash; the belt and horse are not enough."
translations.idiomatic: The prince pointed at the coin stacks, called Jiji by his pet name, and told Chengye, "Hege needs money. Seventh Brother, you ought to give him one whole pile—the belt and horse aren't enough.

sentences.zh: 承業曰：「郎君纏頭皆出承業俸祿，此錢，大王所以養戰士也，承業不敢以公物為私禮。」

translations.literal: Chengye said, "The young lord's gift money all comes from Chengye's salary. This money is what Your Highness uses to support the warriors. Chengye dare not use public goods as a private gift."
translations.idiomatic: Chengye replied, "The boy's gift money comes from my own salary. This treasury money is for feeding your soldiers. I dare not treat public funds as a private gift.

sentences.zh: 王不悅，憑酒以語侵之，承業怒曰：「僕老敕使耳！

translations.literal: The prince was displeased and, emboldened by wine, spoke to him insultingly. Chengye angrily said, "This old man is but an imperial commissioner!
translations.idiomatic: The prince took offense and, drunk, spoke to him harshly. Chengye flared up: "I am only an old imperial commissioner!

sentences.zh: 非為子孫計，惜此庫錢，所以佐王成霸業也，不然，王自取用之，何問僕為！

translations.literal: It is not for my descendants that I cherish this treasury money—it is to help Your Highness achieve hegemony. Otherwise, take and use it yourself; why ask me at all!
translations.idiomatic: I am not hoarding this money for my heirs—I am saving it to help you build an empire. Otherwise take what you want yourself; why ask me!

sentences.zh: 不過財盡民散，一無所成耳。」

translations.literal: Nothing will come of it but exhausted wealth, a scattered populace, and total failure."
translations.idiomatic: You will only exhaust your treasury, drive the people away, and achieve nothing."

sentences.zh: 王怒，顧李紹榮索劍，承業起，挽王衣泣曰：「僕受先王顧托之命，誓為國家誅汴賊，若以惜庫物死於王手，仆下見先王無愧矣。

translations.literal: The prince grew angry and turned to Li Shaorong to demand a sword. Chengye rose, seized the prince's robe, and wept, saying, "I received the late king's dying charge and swore to destroy the Bian bandits for the state. If I die by Your Highness's hand for guarding the treasury, I can face the late king without shame.
translations.idiomatic: The prince flew into a rage and called to Li Shaorong for a sword. Chengye rose, clutched the prince's robe, and wept: "Your father entrusted me on his deathbed to destroy the Bian usurpers. If I die by your hand for guarding the treasury, I can face him without shame.

sentences.zh: 今日就王請死！」

translations.literal: Today I ask Your Highness to grant me death!"
translations.idiomatic: Today I ask you to kill me!"

sentences.zh: 閻寶從旁解承業手令退，承業奮拳毆寶踣地，罵曰：「閻寶，朱溫之黨，受晉大恩，曾不盡忠為報，顧欲以諂媚自容邪！」

translations.literal: Yan Bao stepped in from the side, loosened Chengye's hand, and urged him to withdraw. Chengye swung his fist and struck Bao to the ground, cursing, "Yan Bao, you are a follower of Zhu Wen! You received great favor from Jin and have never repaid it with full loyalty—do you mean to save yourself through flattery instead!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bao tried to pull Chengye away. Chengye punched him to the floor and shouted, "Yan Bao, you were Zhu Wen's man! Jin showed you great favor, and you never repaid it with loyal service—do you think flattery will save you!"

sentences.zh: 曹太夫人聞之，遽令召王，王惶恐叩頭，謝承業曰：「吾以酒失忤七哥，必且得罪於太夫人，七哥為吾痛飲以分其過。」

translations.literal: When Lady Cao heard of it, she immediately sent for the prince. The prince, in fear, kowtowed and apologized to Chengye, saying, "I offended Seventh Brother in a drunken lapse and am sure to have displeased the Lady. Seventh Brother, drink deeply for my sake to share the blame."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cao sent for the prince at once. Terrified, he kowtowed and apologized to Chengye: "I offended you in my cups and have surely displeased the Lady. Seventh Brother, drink with me and share the fault."

sentences.zh: 王連飲四卮，承業竟不肯飲。

translations.literal: The prince drank four cups in succession, but Chengye still refused to drink.
translations.idiomatic: The prince drained four cups in a row, but Chengye would not drink.

sentences.zh: 王入宮，太夫人使人謝承業曰：「小兒忤特進，適已笞之矣。」

translations.literal: The prince entered the inner palace. The Lady sent a messenger to apologize to Chengye, saying, "The boy offended the Special Advancement; I have just had him beaten."
translations.idiomatic: The prince went inside. Lady Cao sent word to Chengye: "The boy offended you, Special Advancement; I have just had him whipped."

sentences.zh: 明日，太夫人與王俱至承業第謝之。

translations.literal: The next day the Lady and the prince both went to Chengye's residence to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Lady Cao and the prince came together to Chengye's house to apologize.

sentences.zh: 未幾，承製授承業開府儀同三司、左衛上將軍、燕國公。

translations.literal: Before long an imperial edict was received appointing Chengye Grandee of Splendid Happiness with the Same Rank as the Three Councillors, General of the Left Guard, and Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict arrived making Chengye Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Rank Equal to the Three Councillors, General of the Left Guard, and Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 承業固辭不受，但稱唐官以至終身。

translations.literal: Chengye firmly declined and would not accept, but used only his Tang titles for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye firmly refused the honors and used only his Tang titles for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 掌書記盧質，嗜酒輕傲，嘗呼王諸弟為豚犬，王銜之。

translations.literal: The chief secretary Lu Zhi was fond of wine and lightly arrogant; he once called the prince's younger brothers pigs and dogs, and the prince harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretary Lu Zhi drank heavily and was insolent; he once called the prince's younger brothers pigs and dogs, and the prince never forgot it.

sentences.zh: 承業恐其及禍，乘間言曰：「盧質數無禮，請為大王殺之。」

translations.literal: Chengye feared he would come to harm and seized an opportunity to say, "Lu Zhi has repeatedly been disrespectful. Please let me kill him for Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Lu would bring disaster on himself, Chengye seized a moment and said, "Lu Zhi has been rude again and again. Let me kill him for you."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「吾方招納賢才以就功業，七哥何言之過也！」

translations.literal: The prince said, "I am just now gathering talented men to accomplish my enterprise—how can Seventh Brother speak so excessively!"
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "I am trying to gather talent to build my enterprise—Seventh Brother, that goes too far!"

sentences.zh: 承業起立賀曰：「王能如此，何憂不得天下！」

translations.literal: Chengye rose and congratulated him, saying, "If Your Highness can be like this, why worry about not gaining the realm under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengye stood and congratulated him: "If you can be like this, what is there to fear about winning the realm!"

sentences.zh: 質由是獲免。

translations.literal: Because of this, Zhi was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi was spared because of that.

sentences.zh: 晉王元妃衛國韓夫人，次燕國伊夫人，次魏國劉夫人。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin's primary consort was Lady Han of Weiguo; next was Lady Yi of Yanguo; next was Lady Liu of Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin's primary consort was Lady Han of Weiguo, followed by Lady Yi of Yanguo and Lady Liu of Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 劉夫人最有寵，其父成安人，以醫卜為業。

translations.literal: Lady Liu was the most favored. Her father was a man of Cheng'an who made his living by medicine and divination.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu was the favorite. Her father was from Cheng'an and earned his living as a physician and diviner.

sentences.zh: 夫人幼時，晉將袁建豐掠得之，入於王宮，性狡悍淫妒，從王在魏。

translations.literal: When the lady was young, the Jin general Yuan Jianfeng captured her and brought her into the princely palace. She was crafty, fierce, licentious, and jealous, and accompanied the prince in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: As a girl she was captured by the Jin general Yuan Jianfeng and taken into the palace. Crafty, fierce, and jealous, she followed the prince to Wei.

sentences.zh: 父聞其貴，詣魏宮上謁，王召袁建豐示之。

translations.literal: When her father heard she had risen in rank, he went to the Wei palace to pay his respects. The prince summoned Yuan Jianfeng to show him to her.
translations.idiomatic: When her father heard she had risen high, he came to the Wei palace to see her. The prince summoned Yuan Jianfeng to identify him.

sentences.zh: 建豐曰：「始得夫人時，有黃須丈人護之，此是也。」

translations.literal: Jianfeng said, "When I first obtained the lady, a yellow-bearded old man was protecting her—this is he."
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng said, "When I first took her, a yellow-bearded old man was guarding her—this is the man."

sentences.zh: 王以語夫人，夫人方與諸夫人爭寵，以門地相高，恥其家寒微，大怒曰：「妾去鄉時略可記憶，妾父不幸死亂兵，妾守屍哭之而去，今何物田舍翁敢至此！」

translations.literal: The prince told the lady. She was then contending with the other ladies for favor and vying over family status; ashamed that her family was humble, she flew into a rage and said, "When I left my home village I can still remember clearly—my father unhappily died among the disorderly troops, and I stayed by his corpse weeping before I left. What sort of rustic old man dares come here now!"
translations.idiomatic: The prince told her. She was then vying with the other consorts over rank and was ashamed of her humble origins. She flew into a rage: "I still remember leaving home—my father died in the chaos, and I wept over his body before I left. What kind of country bumpkin dares show his face here!"

sentences.zh: 命笞劉叟於宮門。

translations.literal: She ordered the old man Liu to be flogged at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered the old man Liu beaten at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 越王巖遣客省使劉瑭使於吳，告即位，且勸吳王稱帝。

translations.literal: The King of Yue, Yan, sent the guest-reception commissioner Liu Tang as envoy to Wu to announce his accession and also to urge the King of Wu to declare himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: King Yan of Yue sent guest-reception commissioner Liu Tang to Wu to announce his enthronement and urge the King of Wu to declare himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 閏月，戊申，蜀主以判內樞密院庾凝績為吏部尚書、內樞密使。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day wushen, the ruler of Shu appointed Yu Ningji, who administered the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs, Minister of Personnel and Commissioner of the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on wushen, the Shu ruler made Yu Ningji, administrator of the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs, Minister of Personnel and Commissioner of the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙子朔，日南至，蜀主祀圜丘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day bingzi, the sun reached its southern extreme. The ruler of Shu sacrificed at the Round Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month, bingzi, the winter solstice, the Shu ruler sacrificed at the Round Altar.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞河冰合，曰：「用兵數歲，限一水不得渡，今冰自合，天讚我也。」

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin heard that the river ice had frozen solid, he said, "For years in campaigning we were blocked by this one river and could not cross. Now the ice has joined of itself—Heaven approves me."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin heard the river had frozen over, he said, "For years this river kept us from crossing. Now the ice has joined by itself—Heaven favors me."

sentences.zh: 亟如魏州。

translations.literal: He hurried to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀主以劉知俊為都招討使，諸將皆舊功臣，多不用其命，且疾之，故無成功。

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu had made Liu Zhijun overall commander for pacification, but the generals were all old meritorious officials; many did not obey his orders and moreover resented him, so there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler had made Liu Zhijun overall commander for pacification, but the generals were old meritocrats who often ignored his orders and resented him, so he achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 唐文扆數毀之，蜀主亦忌其才，嘗謂所親曰：「吾老矣，知俊非爾輩所能馭民。」

translations.literal: Tang Wenyi repeatedly slandered him, and the ruler of Shu also envied his talent. He once said to those close to him, "I am old. Zhijun is not someone you people can control."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Wenyi kept slandering him, and the Shu ruler also feared his ability. He once told his intimates, "I am old. Zhijun is not someone you can control."

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛亥，收知俊，稱其謀叛，斬於炭市。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xinhai, Zhijun was arrested on the charge of plotting rebellion and executed at Tanshi Market.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinhai, Zhijun was arrested for alleged treason and executed at Tanshi Market.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，蜀大赦，改明年元曰光天。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Shu proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the next year's era name to Guangtian.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Shu proclaimed a general amnesty and set the next year's era name to Guangtian.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以張宗奭為天下兵馬副元帥。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Zhang Zongbi was made Deputy Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Zhang Zongbi was made Deputy Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 帝論平慶州功，丁卯，以左龍虎統軍賀瑰為宣義節度使、同平章事，尋以為北面行營招討使。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed the merit in pacifying Qingzhou. On the day dingmao, He Gui, commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, was made military governor of Xuanyi and Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs, and soon afterward was made commander for pacification of the northern expeditionary camp.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the pacification of Qingzhou, the emperor on dingmao made He Gui, commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, military governor of Xuanyi and Co-Director, and soon named him commander of the northern expeditionary camp.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，晉王畋於朝城。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, the Prince of Jin hunted at Chaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the Prince of Jin hunted at Chaocheng.

sentences.zh: 是日，大寒，晉王視河冰已堅，引步騎稍度。

translations.literal: That day was bitterly cold. The prince saw that the river ice was already firm and led infantry and cavalry to cross little by little.
translations.idiomatic: That day was fiercely cold. Seeing the ice firm, the prince led foot and horse across bit by bit.

sentences.zh: 梁甲士三千戍楊劉城，緣河數十里，列柵相望，晉王急攻，皆陷之。

translations.literal: Three thousand Liang armored troops garrisoned Yangliu City; for several tens of li along the river, palisades stood facing one another. The Prince of Jin attacked urgently and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand Liang armored troops held Yangliu City, with palisades strung along the river for miles. The prince attacked hard and took them all.

sentences.zh: 進攻楊劉城，使步卒斬其鹿角，負葭葦塞塹，四面進攻，即日拔之，獲其守將安彥之。

translations.literal: He pressed the attack on Yangliu City, had infantry cut down the chevaux-de-frise, carry reeds to fill the moat, and assault from all four sides. That same day the city was taken, and its defending general An Yanzhi was captured.
translations.idiomatic: He assaulted Yangliu City itself, had infantry cut the chevaux-de-frise, pack reeds into the moat, and attack from all sides. The city fell the same day, and its commander An Yanzhi was captured.

sentences.zh: 先是，租庸使、戶部尚書趙巖言於帝曰：「陛下踐祚以來，尚未南郊，議者以為無異籓侯，為四方所輕。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Commissioner of Tax and Corvée, Minister of Revenue Zhao Yan, said to the emperor, "Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, you have not yet performed the southern suburban sacrifice. Commentators say this makes you no different from a feudal lord and that the four quarters hold you lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, tax commissioner and Minister of Revenue Zhao Yan told the emperor, "Since you took the throne you have not performed the southern suburban rite. Critics say you look no different from a feudal lord, and the realm holds you lightly.

sentences.zh: 請幸西都行郊禮，遂謁宣陵。」

translations.literal: I ask that you visit the western capital to perform the suburban rite and then pay homage at the Xuan Mausoleum."
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to go to the western capital for the suburban rite and then visit the Xuan Mausoleum."

sentences.zh: 敬翔諫曰：「自劉鏐失利以來，公私困竭，人心惴恐；

translations.literal: Jing Xiang remonstrated, saying, "Since Liu Zhen's defeat, public and private resources have been exhausted and hearts are fearful and alarmed;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang objected: "Since Liu Zhen's defeat, public and private coffers are drained and people live in fear;

sentences.zh: 今展禮圜丘，必行賞賚，是慕虛名而受實弊也。

translations.literal: if you now perform the Round Altar rite, rewards and gifts must follow. That is to covet empty reputation while suffering real harm.
translations.idiomatic: if you hold the Round Altar ceremony now, lavish rewards must follow. You would chase empty prestige at real cost.

sentences.zh: 且勍敵近在河上，乘輿豈宜輕動！

translations.literal: Moreover, a formidable enemy is close on the river—how can the imperial carriage be lightly moved!
translations.idiomatic: And a formidable enemy is right on the river—how can the throne travel lightly!

sentences.zh: 俟北方既平，報本未晚。」

translations.literal: Wait until the north is pacified; it will not be too late to repay the root."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the north is secure; repaying Heaven's favor can come later."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，己巳，如洛陽，閱車服，飾宮闕，郊祀有日，聞楊劉失守，道路訛言晉軍已入大梁，扼汜水矣，從官皆憂其家，相顧涕泣。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen. On the day jisi he went to Luoyang, inspected chariots and regalia, and adorned the palace halls. The suburban sacrifice was set for a fixed day when word came that Yangliu had fallen. Rumors on the road said the Jin army had already entered Daliang and was holding Sishui. The attendants all worried for their families and looked at one another in tears.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to listen. On jisi he went to Luoyang, reviewed chariots and regalia, and refurbished the palace. The rite was nearly at hand when news came that Yangliu had fallen. Travelers said the Jin army was already in Daliang and holding Sishui. Attendants feared for their families and wept together.

sentences.zh: 帝惶駭失圖，遂罷郊祀，奔歸大梁。

translations.literal: The emperor, panicked and at a loss, canceled the suburban sacrifice and fled back to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Panicked and helpless, the emperor canceled the rite and raced back to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以河南尹張宗奭為西都留守。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, Zhang Zongbi, Prefect of Henan, was made western capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Zhang Zongbi, Prefect of Henan, was made regent of the western capital.

sentences.zh: 是歲，閩王審知為其子牙內都指揮使延鈞娶越主巖之女。

translations.literal: That year, Wang Shenzhi, King of Min, had his son Yanjun, commander of the Inner Palace Guard, marry the daughter of the ruler of Yue, Yan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Min king Wang Shenzhi had his son Yanjun, commander of the Inner Palace Guard, marry the daughter of Yue ruler Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥朔，蜀大赦，復國號曰蜀。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the first day yihai, Shu proclaimed a general amnesty and restored the state name to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, yihai, Shu proclaimed a general amnesty and restored the state name to Shu.

sentences.zh: 帝至大梁，晉兵侵掠至鄆、濮而還。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Daliang, Jin troops raided as far as Yun and Pu and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Daliang, Jin forces raided as far as Yun and Pu and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 敬翔上疏曰：「國家連年喪師，疆土日蹙。

translations.literal: Jing Xiang submitted a memorial saying, "The state has lost armies year after year, and the territory shrinks daily.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang submitted a memorial: "The state has lost armies year after year, and our territory shrinks daily.

sentences.zh: 陛下居深宮之中，所與計事者皆左右近習，豈能量敵國之勝負乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwells deep within the palace, and those with whom you consult on affairs are all close attendants—how can you measure the enemy state's victories and defeats!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty lives deep in the palace and plans only with close attendants—how can you judge the enemy's strength!

sentences.zh: 先帝之時，奄有河北，親御豪傑之將，猶不得志。

translations.literal: In the late emperor's time, when he held all of Hebei and personally commanded heroic generals, he still could not achieve his aim.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the late emperor held all Hebei and led his best generals in person, he could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 今敵至鄆州，陛下不能留意。

translations.literal: Now the enemy has reached Yunzhou, yet Your Majesty cannot give it attention.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy is at Yunzhou, and Your Majesty pays no heed.

sentences.zh: 臣聞李亞子繼位以來，於今十年，攻城野戰，無不親當矢石，近者攻楊劉，身負束薪為士卒先，一鼓拔之。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that since Li Yazi succeeded to the throne, ten years have passed. In storming cities and fighting in the field, he has never failed to face arrows and stones in person. Recently, in attacking Yangliu, he carried a bundle of firewood on his back to lead the troops and took the city at the first assault.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that in the ten years since Li Yazi took the throne he has always faced arrows and stones himself in every siege and battle. At Yangliu he bore firewood on his back to lead the assault and took the city at the first rush.

sentences.zh: 陛下儒雅守文，晏安自若，使賀瑰輩敵之，而望攘逐寇仇，非臣所知也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is refined and literary, keeping to written norms, at ease and self-possessed, and you set men like He Gui against the enemy yet hope to drive off the bandit foe—this is beyond what your servant can understand.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a scholar who keeps to the written way, at ease in the palace, and you send men like He Gui to fight the enemy yet expect to drive off the invaders—that is beyond my understanding.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜詢訪黎老，別求異策。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to consult the common people and elders and seek a different strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should consult the people and seek another plan.

sentences.zh: 不然，憂未艾也。

translations.literal: Otherwise, the troubles will not end.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise our troubles will never end.

sentences.zh: 臣雖駑怯，受國重恩，陛下必若乏才，乞於邊垂自效。」

translations.literal: Though your servant is dull and timid, I have received great favor from the state. If Your Majesty truly lacks talent, I beg to serve on the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Though I am slow and timid, I owe the state a great debt. If Your Majesty lacks capable men, I beg to serve on the frontier."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，趙、張之徒言翔怨望，帝遂不用。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Zhao, Zhang, and their faction said Xiang was resentful and discontent, and the emperor therefore did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Zhao, Zhang, and their faction claimed Xiang was disgruntled, and the emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 吳以右都押牙王祺為虔州行營都指揮使，將洪、撫、袁、吉之兵擊譚全播。

translations.literal: Wu appointed Wang Qi, Right Chief Adjutant, commander of the Qianzhou expeditionary camp and led troops from Hong, Fu, Yuan, and Ji to attack Tan Quanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Wu made Wang Qi, Right Chief Adjutant, commander of the Qianzhou expedition and sent troops from Hong, Fu, Yuan, and Ji against Tan Quanbo.

sentences.zh: 嚴可求以厚利募贛石水工，故吳兵奄至虔州城下，虔人始知之。

translations.literal: Yan Keqiu recruited Gan River boatmen with rich rewards, so Wu troops suddenly arrived beneath the walls of Qianzhou before the people of Qian knew it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Keqiu hired Gan River boatmen with rich rewards, so Wu troops appeared suddenly beneath Qianzhou's walls before the city knew they were coming.

sentences.zh: 蜀太子衍好酒色，樂遊戲。

translations.literal: The crown prince of Shu, Yan, was fond of wine and women and delighted in games.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's crown prince Yan loved wine, women, and play.

sentences.zh: 蜀主嘗自夾城過，聞太子與諸王鬥雞擊球喧呼之聲，歎曰：「吾百戰以立基業，此輩其能守之乎！」

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu once passed through the walled corridor and heard the crown prince and the princes shouting over cockfighting and ball games. He sighed and said, "I established this foundation through a hundred battles—can these fellows hold it!"
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the palace corridor one day, the Shu ruler heard the crown prince and the princes shouting over cockfights and ball games. He sighed: "I built this realm in a hundred battles—can these boys keep it!

sentences.zh: 由是惡張格，而徐賢妃為之內主，竟不能去也。

translations.literal: From this he came to dislike Zhang Ge, but the Worthy Consort Xu acted as his patron within the palace, and in the end he could not remove him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he hated Zhang Ge, but Worthy Consort Xu protected him from within, and the ruler could never remove him.

sentences.zh: 信王宗傑有才略，屢陳時政，蜀主賢之，有廢立意。

translations.literal: Prince Xin Zongjie had talent and strategy, repeatedly offered views on current affairs, and the ruler of Shu admired him and had the intention of deposing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin Zongjie was talented and often spoke on affairs of state. The Shu ruler admired him and considered replacing the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸亥，宗傑暴卒，蜀主深疑之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day guihai, Zongjie died suddenly, and the ruler of Shu deeply suspected foul play.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guihai, Zongjie died suddenly, and the Shu ruler strongly suspected murder.

sentences.zh: 河陽節度使、北面行營排陳使謝彥章將兵數萬攻楊劉城。

translations.literal: Xie Yanzhang, military governor of Heyang and battle-line commander of the northern expeditionary camp, led tens of thousands of troops to attack Yangliu City.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yanzhang, military governor of Heyang and northern battle-line commander, led tens of thousands of men against Yangliu City.

sentences.zh: 甲子，晉王自魏州輕騎詣河上。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the Prince of Jin rode lightly from Weizhou to the Yellow River front.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the Prince of Jin rode lightly from Weizhou to the river front.

sentences.zh: 彥章築壘自固，決河水，瀰浸數里，以限晉兵，晉兵不得進。

translations.literal: Yanzhang built fortifications to secure himself, broke the river banks, and flooded several li to block the Jin troops, who could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang fortified his position, broke the river banks, and flooded several li to block the Jin advance.

sentences.zh: 彥章，許州人也。

translations.literal: Yanzhang was a man of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang was from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 安彥之散卒多聚於兗、鄆山谷為群盜，以觀二國成敗，晉王招募之，多降於晉。

translations.literal: The scattered troops of An Yanzhi gathered in the hills and valleys of Yan and Yun as bandit bands, watching the two states' fortunes. The Prince of Jin recruited them, and many surrendered to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: An Yanzhi's scattered soldiers gathered as bandits in the hills of Yan and Yun, waiting to see which side would win. The Prince of Jin recruited them, and many defected.

sentences.zh: 己亥，蜀主以東面招討使王宗侃為東、西兩路諸軍都統。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, the ruler of Shu made Wang Zongkan, commander for pacification on the east front, overall commander of all armies on the eastern and western routes.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the Shu ruler made Wang Zongkan, eastern pacification commander, overall commander of the eastern and western armies.

sentences.zh: 三月，吳越王鏐初立元帥府，置官屬。

translations.literal: In the third month, Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, first established a marshal's headquarters and appointed its staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, established a marshal's headquarters and appointed its staff.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸卯朔，蜀主立子宗平為忠王，宗特為資王。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day guimao, the ruler of Shu enfeoffed his son Zongping as Prince of Zhong and Zongte as Prince of Zi.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the first day of the fourth month, guimao, the Shu ruler enfeoffed his son Zongping as Prince of Zhong and Zongte as Prince of Zi.

sentences.zh: 岐王復遣使求好於蜀。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi again sent envoys seeking friendship with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi again sent envoys seeking peace with Shu.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以吏部侍郎蕭頃為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, Xiao Qing, Vice Minister of Personnel, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Xiao Qing, Vice Minister of Personnel, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Director.

sentences.zh: 保大節度使高萬金卒。

translations.literal: Gao Wanjin, military governor of Baoda, died.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wanjin, military governor of Baoda, died.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以忠義節度使高萬興兼保大節度使，並鎮鄜、延。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Gao Wanxing, military governor of Zhongyi, was also made military governor of Baoda, governing both Yan and Yan together.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Gao Wanxing, military governor of Zhongyi, was also made military governor of Baoda, holding both Yan and Yan.

sentences.zh: 司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事趙光逢告老，己巳，以司徒致仕。

translations.literal: Zhao Guangfeng, Minister of Works and concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs, requested retirement on grounds of age. On the day jisi he was granted retirement with the rank of Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guangfeng, Minister of Works and Co-Director, requested retirement. On jisi he was granted retirement as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 蜀主自永平末得疾，昏瞀，至是增劇。

translations.literal: Since the end of the Yongping era the ruler of Shu had been ill, dim-eyed and confused, and by this time it had grown worse.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler had been ill since late Yongping, his sight dim and his mind clouded, and now it grew worse.

sentences.zh: 以北面行營招討使兼中書令王宗弼沉靜有謀，五月，召還，以為馬步都指揮使。

translations.literal: Because Wang Zongbi, commander for pacification of the northern expeditionary camp and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, was calm and resourceful, in the fifth month he was recalled and made overall commander of cavalry and infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongbi, northern pacification commander and Director of the Secretariat, was calm and shrewd. In the fifth month he was recalled and made overall commander of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，召大臣入寢殿，告之曰：「太子仁弱，朕不能違諸公之請，逾次而立之。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, he summoned the great ministers into the sleeping hall and told them, "The crown prince is benevolent but weak. I could not refuse your request and set him up out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai he summoned the ministers to his sickroom and said, "The crown prince is gentle but weak. I could not refuse your request and made him heir out of turn.

sentences.zh: 若其不堪大業，可置諸別宮，幸勿殺之。

translations.literal: If he cannot bear the great enterprise, you may place him in a separate palace—please do not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot bear the throne, place him in a separate palace, but do not kill him.

sentences.zh: 但王氏子弟，諸公擇而輔之。

translations.literal: As for the Wang clan youths, choose among them and support one.
translations.idiomatic: Choose one of the Wang princes and support him.

sentences.zh: 徐妃兄弟，止可優其祿位，慎勿使之掌兵預政，以全其宗族。」

translations.literal: The brothers of Consort Xu should receive generous salaries and ranks only; take care not to let them command troops or take part in government, so as to preserve their clan."
translations.idiomatic: Give Consort Xu's brothers generous salaries and ranks only. Do not let them command troops or govern, so their clan may survive."

sentences.zh: 內飛龍使唐文扆久典禁兵，參預機密，欲去諸大臣，遣人守宮門。

translations.literal: The Inner Flying Dragon Commissioner Tang Wenyi had long controlled the palace guard and taken part in secret affairs. He wished to remove the great ministers and posted men to guard the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Flying Dragon Commissioner Tang Wenyi had long controlled the palace guard and secret affairs. He wanted the great ministers removed and posted guards at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 王宗弼等三十餘人日至朝堂，不得入見，文扆屢以蜀主之命慰撫之，伺蜀主殂，即作難。

translations.literal: Wang Zongbi and more than thirty others came daily to the court hall but could not enter to be received. Wenyi repeatedly comforted them in the ruler of Shu's name, waiting for the ruler's death to raise trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongbi and more than thirty others came daily to court but were barred from audience. Wenyi kept reassuring them in the ruler's name, waiting to move once the ruler died.

sentences.zh: 遣其黨內皇城使潘在迎偵察外事，在迎以其謀告宗弼等。

translations.literal: He sent his follower Pan Zaiying, commissioner of the Inner Imperial City, to spy on outside affairs. Zaiying reported the plot to Zongbi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his man Pan Zaiying, commissioner of the Inner Imperial City, to watch outside affairs. Zaiying told Zongbi and the others of the plot.

sentences.zh: 宗弼等排闥入，言文扆之罪，以天冊府掌書記崔延昌權判六軍事，召太子入侍疾。

translations.literal: Zongbi and the others forced the doors open and entered, denounced Wenyi's crimes, made Cui Yanchang, secretary of the Celestial Register Office, provisional administrator of the Six Armies, and summoned the crown prince to attend the illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi and the others forced their way in, denounced Wenyi, made Cui Yanchang of the Celestial Register Office provisional commander of the Six Armies, and summoned the crown prince to the sickbed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，貶唐文扆為眉州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Tang Wenyi was demoted to prefect of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Tang Wenyi was demoted to prefect of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士承旨王保晦坐附會文扆，削官爵，流瀘州。

translations.literal: Wang Baohui, Hanlin Academician Expositor, was punished for associating with Wenyi: his rank and titles were stripped and he was banished to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Baohui, Hanlin Academician Expositor, was stripped of rank for siding with Wenyi and exiled to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 在迎，炕之子也。

translations.literal: Zaiying was the son of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiying was Kang's son.

sentences.zh: 丙申，蜀主詔中外財賦、中書除授、諸司刑獄案牘專委庾凝績，都城及行營軍旅之事委宣徽南院使宋光嗣。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, the ruler of Shu decreed that domestic and foreign revenues, Secretariat appointments, and legal records of all offices were entrusted solely to Yu Ningji, and affairs of the capital and expeditionary camps to Song Guangsi, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the Shu ruler entrusted all revenues, Secretariat appointments, and legal records to Yu Ningji, and capital and camp military affairs to Song Guangsi of the Southern Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，削唐文扆官爵，流雅州。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Tang Wenyi's rank and titles were stripped and he was banished to Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Tang Wenyi was stripped of rank and exiled to Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以宋光嗣為內樞密使，與兼中書令王宗弼、宗瑤、宗綰、宗夔並受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Song Guangsi was made Commissioner of the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs, and together with Wang Zongbi, Zongyao, Zongwan, and Zongkui, who also held the post of Director of the Secretariat, he received the dying charge to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Song Guangsi was made Commissioner of the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs and, with Wang Zongbi, Zongyao, Zongwan, and Zongkui, received the dying charge to assist the new ruler.

sentences.zh: 初，蜀主雖因唐制置樞密使，專用士人，及唐文扆得罪，蜀主以諸將多許州故人，恐其不為幼主用，故以光嗣代之。

translations.literal: Earlier, though the ruler of Shu had established the Bureau of Military Affairs following Tang institutions and used scholars exclusively, after Tang Wenyi fell from favor the ruler feared that many generals were old associates from Xuzhou and would not serve the young ruler, so he replaced Wenyi with Guangsi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Shu ruler had followed Tang practice and staffed the Bureau of Military Affairs with scholars. After Wenyi's fall he feared the generals, many old Xuzhou associates, would not serve the young ruler, and replaced Wenyi with Guangsi.

sentences.zh: 自是宦者始用事。

translations.literal: From this time eunuchs began to hold power.
translations.idiomatic: From then on eunuchs began to wield power.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬寅朔，蜀主殂。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day renyin, the ruler of Shu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day renyin, the Shu ruler died.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, the crown prince assumed the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the crown prince took the throne.

sentences.zh: 尊徐賢妃為太后、徐淑妃為太妃。

translations.literal: The Worthy Consort Xu was honored as Empress Dowager and the Graceful Consort Xu as Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort Xu was made Empress Dowager and Graceful Consort Xu Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 以宋光嗣判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: Song Guangsi was made administrator of the Six Armies and all guard units.
translations.idiomatic: Song Guangsi was put in charge of the Six Armies and palace guards.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，殺唐文扆、王保晦。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, Tang Wenyi and Wang Baohui were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Tang Wenyi and Wang Baohui were executed.

sentences.zh: 命西面招討副使王宗昱殺天雄節度使唐文裔於秦州，免左保勝軍使領右街使唐道崇官。

translations.literal: He ordered Wang Zongyu, deputy commander for pacification on the west front, to kill Tang Wenyi, military governor of Tianxiong, at Qinzhou, and stripped Tang Daozong, commander of the Left Victorious Guard Army and Right Street Commissioner, of his posts.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered western deputy commander Wang Zongyu to kill Tang Wenyi, military governor of Tianxiong, at Qinzhou, and stripped Tang Daozong, commander of the Left Victorious Guard and Right Street Commissioner, of his posts.

sentences.zh: 吳內外馬步都軍使、昌化節度使、同平章事徐知訓，驕倨淫暴。

translations.literal: Xu Zhixun of Wu, overall commander of inner and outer cavalry and infantry, military governor of Changhua, and Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs, was arrogant, insolent, licentious, and violent.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhixun of Wu, overall army commander, military governor of Changhua, and Co-Director, was arrogant, licentious, and brutal.

sentences.zh: 威武節度使、知撫州李德誠有家妓數十，知訓求之，德誠遣使謝曰：「家之所有皆長年，或有子，不足以侍貴人，當更為公求少而美者。」

translations.literal: Li Decheng, military governor of Weiwu and acting prefect of Fuzhou, had several dozen household entertainers. Zhixun demanded them. Decheng sent a messenger to decline, saying, "All that my household has are older women, some with children. They are not fit to serve a noble person. I shall seek younger and more beautiful ones for you."
translations.idiomatic: Li Decheng, military governor of Weiwu and acting prefect of Fuzhou, had dozens of household entertainers. Zhixun demanded them. Decheng sent word: "All mine are older women, some with children—not fit for a noble lord. I will find younger and prettier ones for you.

sentences.zh: 知訓怒，謂使者曰：「會當殺德誠，並其妻取之！」

translations.literal: Zhixun flew into a rage and told the messenger, "The day will come when I kill Decheng and take his wife too!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun raged and told the messenger, "One day I'll kill Decheng and take his wife too!

sentences.zh: 知訓狎侮吳王，無復君臣之禮。

translations.literal: Zhixun treated the King of Wu with familiar contempt and no longer observed the rites between ruler and subject.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun treated the King of Wu with open contempt and no longer observed court decorum.

sentences.zh: 嘗與王為優，自為參軍，使王為蒼鶻，總角弊衣執帽以從。

translations.literal: He once performed comic opera with the king, playing the straight man himself and making the king play the buffoon, with hair in knots, in shabby clothes, holding a cap and following along.
translations.idiomatic: He once put on a comic play with the king, playing the straight man while making the king play the buffoon in shabby clothes with hair in knots, cap in hand.

sentences.zh: 又嘗泛舟濁河，王先起，知訓以彈彈之。

translations.literal: Another time they boated on the Zhuo River. When the king rose first, Zhixun hit him with a pellet.
translations.idiomatic: Another time they boated on the Zhuo River. When the king got up first, Zhixun shot him with a pellet.

sentences.zh: 又嘗賞花於禪智寺，知訓使酒悖慢，王懼而泣，四座股慄。

translations.literal: Another time they viewed flowers at Chanzhisi Temple. Zhixun, drunk, was rude and insolent. The king, in fear, wept, and everyone present trembled in their seats.
translations.idiomatic: Another time at Chanzhisi Temple he got drunk and insulted the king, who wept in fear while everyone present trembled.

sentences.zh: 左右扶王登舟，知訓乘輕舟逐之，不及，以鐵撾殺王親吏。

translations.literal: Attendants helped the king aboard his boat. Zhixun took a light boat in pursuit but could not catch up, and killed one of the king's personal attendants with an iron mace.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants helped the king aboard. Zhixun chased in a light boat but could not catch him and killed one of the king's personal attendants with an iron mace.

sentences.zh: 將佐無敢言者，父溫皆不之知。

translations.literal: None of the officers and aides dared speak of it, and his father Wen knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: No officer dared speak of it, and his father Wen knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 知訓及弟知詢皆不禮於徐知誥，獨季弟知諫以兄事禮之。

translations.literal: Zhixun and his brother Zhixun both treated Xu Zhigao without courtesy; only the youngest brother Zhijian treated him with the rites due an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun and his brother Zhixun both treated Xu Zhigao rudely; only the youngest brother Zhijian treated him as an elder.

sentences.zh: 知訓嘗召兄弟飲，知誥不至，知訓怒曰：「乞子不欲酒，欲劍乎！」

translations.literal: Zhixun once summoned his brothers to drink. Zhigao did not come. Zhixun angrily said, "Does the beggar's son want wine—or a sword!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun once summoned his brothers to drink. When Zhigao did not come, Zhixun raged: "Does the beggar's son want wine—or a sword!

sentences.zh: 又嘗與知誥飲，伏甲欲殺之，知諫躡知誥足，知誥陽起如廁，遁去，知訓以劍授左右刁彥能使追殺之。

translations.literal: Another time he drank with Zhigao, hid armed men intending to kill him, and Zhijian trod on Zhigao's foot. Zhigao pretended to rise to the privy and escaped. Zhixun gave a sword to his attendant Diao Yanneng and sent him to pursue and kill Zhigao.
translations.idiomatic: Another time he drank with Zhigao and hid armed men to kill him. Zhijian trod on Zhigao's foot; Zhigao pretended to go to the privy and escaped. Zhixun gave a sword to Diao Yanneng and sent him to kill Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 彥能馳騎及於中塗，舉劍示知誥而還，以不及告。

translations.literal: Yanneng rode hard and caught Zhigao midway, raised the sword to show him, then returned and reported that he had not caught up.
translations.idiomatic: Yanneng rode hard, caught Zhigao on the road, showed him the sword, then returned and reported he had failed.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使、同平章事、諸道副都統朱瑾遣家妓通候問於知訓，知訓強欲私之，瑾已不平。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin, military governor of Pinglu, Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs, and deputy overall commander of all circuits, sent a household entertainer to convey greetings to Zhixun. Zhixun forcibly sought to take her privately, and Jin was already displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin, military governor of Pinglu, Co-Director, and deputy overall commander, sent a household entertainer to greet Zhixun. Zhixun tried to take her by force, and Jin was already angry.

sentences.zh: 知訓惡瑾位加己上，置靜淮軍於泗州，出瑾為靜淮節度使，瑾益恨之，然外事知訓愈謹。

translations.literal: Zhixun resented that Jin's rank was above his own. He established the Jinghuai Army at Sizhou and transferred Jin out as military governor of Jinghuai. Jin hated him all the more, yet in outward affairs he treated Zhixun with increasing deference.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun resented Jin's higher rank. He established the Jinghuai Army at Sizhou and transferred Jin there as military governor. Jin hated him more but outwardly treated him with greater deference.

sentences.zh: 瑾有所愛馬，冬貯於幄，夏貯於幬。

translations.literal: Jin had a beloved horse, stabled in winter in a tent and in summer in a canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had a beloved horse housed in a tent in winter and under a canopy in summer.

sentences.zh: 寵妓有絕色。

translations.literal: His favored entertainer was of unsurpassed beauty.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite entertainer was a woman of rare beauty.

sentences.zh: 知訓過別瑾，瑾置酒，自捧觴，出寵妓使歌，以所愛馬為壽，知訓大喜。

translations.literal: When Zhixun came to visit Jin on his way elsewhere, Jin set out wine, personally raised the cup, brought out his favored entertainer to sing, and offered his beloved horse as a toast-gift. Zhixun was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixun stopped to visit Jin, Jin set out wine, raised the cup himself, had his favorite entertainer sing, and offered his beloved horse as a gift. Zhixun was delighted.

sentences.zh: 瑾因延之中堂，伏壯士於戶內，出妻陶氏拜之。

translations.literal: Jin then invited him into the central hall, hid strong men inside the doorway, and brought out his wife, Lady Tao, to bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then invited him into the central hall, hid strong men inside the doorway, and brought out his wife Lady Tao to bow to him.

sentences.zh: 知訓答拜，瑾以笏自後擊之踣地，呼壯士出斬之。

translations.literal: Zhixun returned the bow. Jin struck him from behind with his tablet and knocked him to the ground, then called the strong men out to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun returned the bow. Jin struck him from behind with his tablet, knocked him down, and had his men behead him.

sentences.zh: 瑾先系二悍馬於廡下，將圖知訓，密令人解縱之，馬相蹄嚙，聲甚厲，以是外人莫之聞。

translations.literal: Jin had first tied two fierce horses beneath the corridor. As he was about to move against Zhixun, he secretly had men release them. The horses kicked and bit each other with loud noise, so outsiders heard nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had tied two fierce horses beneath the corridor. Before moving against Zhixun he had them released; they kicked and bit each other loudly, so no one outside heard.

sentences.zh: 瑾提知訓首出，知訓從者數百人皆散走。

translations.literal: Jin carried Zhixun's head out, and Zhixun's several hundred followers all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jin carried out Zhixun's head, and his several hundred followers fled.

sentences.zh: 瑾馳入府，以首示吳王曰：「僕已為大王除害！」

translations.literal: Jin galloped into the headquarters and showed the head to the King of Wu, saying, "Your servant has removed the harm for Your Highness!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin galloped into headquarters and showed the head to the King of Wu: "I have removed the threat for you!

sentences.zh: 王懼，以衣障面，走入內，曰：「舅自為之，我不敢知！」

translations.literal: The king, in fear, covered his face with his robe, ran inside, and said, "Uncle, do as you will—I dare not know!"
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the king covered his face and ran inside: "Uncle, do as you will—I want no part of this!

sentences.zh: 瑾曰：「婢子不足與成大事！」

translations.literal: Jin said, "This weakling is not fit to accomplish great things!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "This weakling is not fit for great things!

sentences.zh: 以知訓首擊柱，挺劍將出，子城使翟虔等已闔府門勒兵討之，乃自後逾城，墜而折足，顧追者曰：「吾為萬人除害，以一身任患。」

translations.literal: He struck the pillar with Zhixun's head, drew his sword, and was about to go out when Zhai Qian and others, commissioners of the inner city, had already closed the headquarters gates and marshaled troops against him. He then climbed over the rear wall, fell and broke his foot, turned to his pursuers and said, "I removed harm for ten thousand men and take the blame upon myself alone."
translations.idiomatic: He struck a pillar with Zhixun's head, drew his sword, and was about to leave when Zhai Qian and others had closed the gates and raised troops against him. He climbed the rear wall, fell and broke his foot, and told his pursuers: "I removed a scourge for the people and take the blame alone.

sentences.zh: 遂自剄。

translations.literal: Then he cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Then he cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 徐知誥在潤州聞難，用宋齊丘策，即日引兵濟江。

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao, at Runzhou, heard of the crisis and, following Song Qiqiu's plan, that same day led troops across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao at Runzhou heard of the crisis and, following Song Qiqiu's advice, crossed the river with troops the same day.

sentences.zh: 瑾已死，因撫定軍府。

translations.literal: Jin was already dead, so he pacified and secured the military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was already dead, and Zhigao pacified the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時徐溫諸子皆弱，溫乃以知誥代知訓執吳政，沉朱瑾屍於雷塘而滅其族。

translations.literal: At the time all of Xu Wen's sons were weak. Wen therefore had Zhigao replace Zhixun in governing Wu, sank Zhu Jin's corpse in Leitang, and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen's sons were all weak, so Wen had Zhigao replace Zhixun in governing Wu, sank Zhu Jin's body in Leitang, and exterminated his clan.

sentences.zh: 瑾之殺知訓也，泰寧節度使米志誠從十餘騎問瑾所向，聞其已死，乃歸。

translations.literal: When Jin killed Zhixun, Mi Zhicheng, military governor of Taining, followed with a dozen horsemen to ask where Jin was going. Hearing he was already dead, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin killed Zhixun, Mi Zhicheng, military governor of Taining, followed with a dozen horsemen to find him. Hearing Jin was dead, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 宣諭使李儼貧困，寓居海陵。

translations.literal: Li Yan, imperial proclamation commissioner, was impoverished and lodged at Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, imperial proclamation commissioner, was poor and living at Hailing.

sentences.zh: 溫疑其與瑾通謀，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Wen suspected they had conspired with Jin and had them both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wen suspected they had conspired with Jin and had them both killed.

sentences.zh: 嚴可求恐志誠不受命，詐稱袁州大破楚兵，將吏皆入賀，伏壯士於戟門，擒志誠，斬之，並其諸子。

translations.literal: Yan Keqiu feared Zhicheng would not obey orders. He falsely announced that Yuanzhou had routed Chu troops. When officers and clerks all came to congratulate, he hid strong men at the halberd gate, seized Zhicheng, beheaded him, and killed all his sons as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Keqiu feared Zhicheng would not obey. He falsely announced a great victory at Yuanzhou over Chu. When officers came to congratulate, he hid men at the gate, seized Zhicheng, beheaded him, and killed his sons.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，晉王自魏州勞軍於楊劉，自泛舟測河水，其深沒槍。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, the Prince of Jin came from Weizhou to review the troops at Yangliu. He himself boated out to measure the river water; it was deep enough to cover a spear.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the Prince of Jin came from Weizhou to review troops at Yangliu. He boated out to measure the river—it was deep enough to cover a spear.

sentences.zh: 王謂諸將曰：「梁軍非有戰意，但欲阻水以老我師，當涉水攻之。」

translations.literal: The prince told the generals, "The Liang army has no will to fight; it only wants to block the water to wear down our force. We should wade across and attack."
translations.idiomatic: The prince told his generals, "The Liang army doesn't mean to fight—they only want to use the water to wear us down. We should wade across and attack.

sentences.zh: 甲子，王引親軍先涉，諸軍隨之，褰甲橫槍，結陳而進。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the prince led his personal troops to cross first, and the other armies followed, lifting their armor, spears horizontal, forming battle lines as they advanced.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the prince led his personal troops across first. The other armies followed, armor lifted and spears level, advancing in battle formation.

sentences.zh: 是日水落，深才及膝。

translations.literal: That day the water had fallen; the depth reached only to the knee.
translations.idiomatic: That day the water had fallen to knee depth.

sentences.zh: 匡國節度使、北面行營排陳使謝彥章帥眾臨岸拒之，晉兵不得進，乃稍引卻，梁兵從之。

translations.literal: Xie Yanzhang, military governor of Kuangguo and battle-line commander of the northern expeditionary camp, led his force to the bank to block them. The Jin troops could not advance and therefore withdrew slightly, and the Liang troops followed.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yanzhang, military governor of Kuangguo and northern battle-line commander, blocked them at the bank. The Jin force could not advance and withdrew slightly, and the Liang troops followed.

sentences.zh: 及中流，鼓噪復進，彥章不能支，稍退登岸。

translations.literal: When they reached midstream, with drums and shouts they advanced again. Yanzhang could not hold and withdrew little by little up the bank.
translations.idiomatic: At midstream they advanced again with drums and shouts. Yanzhang could not hold and fell back up the bank.

sentences.zh: 晉兵因而乘之，梁兵大敗，死傷不可勝紀，河水為之赤，彥章僅以身免。

translations.literal: The Jin troops pressed the advantage. The Liang army was routed; dead and wounded were beyond counting, the river water turned red, and Yanzhang barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin troops pressed the attack. The Liang army was routed; casualties were beyond count, the river ran red, and Yanzhang barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 是日，晉人遂陷濱河四寨。

translations.literal: That day the Jin forces took four riverbank camps.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Jin forces captured four riverbank camps.

sentences.zh: 蜀唐文扆既死，太傅、門下侍郎、同平章事張格內不自安，或勸格稱疾俟命，禮部尚書楊玢自恐失勢，謂格曰：「公有援立大功，不足憂也。」

translations.literal: After Tang Wenyi of Shu was dead, Zhang Ge, Grand Mentor, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs, was ill at ease within himself. Some advised Ge to claim illness and await orders. Yang Bin, Minister of Rites, fearing he would lose power himself, told Ge, "Your Grace has great merit in supporting the enthronement—there is no need to worry."
translations.idiomatic: After Tang Wenyi's death, Zhang Ge, Grand Mentor and Co-Director, was uneasy. Some advised him to feign illness and wait. Yang Bin, Minister of Rites, fearing his own fall, told him: "You have great merit in enthroning the new ruler—there is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 庚午，貶格為茂州刺史，玢為榮經尉。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Ge was demoted to prefect of Maozhou and Bin to magistrate of Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Ge was demoted to prefect of Maozhou and Bin to magistrate of Rongjing.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎許寂、戶部侍郎潘嶠皆坐格黨貶官。

translations.literal: Xu Ji, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Pan Qiao, Vice Minister of Revenue, were both punished as Zhang Ge's faction and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Pan Qiao, Vice Minister of Revenue, were demoted as Zhang Ge's allies.

sentences.zh: 格尋再貶維州司戶，庾凝績又奏徙格於合水鎮，令茂州刺史顧承郾伺格陰事。

translations.literal: Ge was soon demoted again to registrar of Weizhou. Yu Ningji also memorialized to transfer Ge to Heshui Town and ordered Gu Chengyan, prefect of Maozhou, to watch for secret matters concerning Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was soon demoted again to registrar of Weizhou. Yu Ningji also had him moved to Heshui Town and ordered Maozhou prefect Gu Chengyan to watch for any secret plots.

sentences.zh: 王宗侃妻以格同姓，欲全之，謂承郾母曰：「戒汝子，勿為人報仇，他日將歸罪於汝。」

translations.literal: Wang Zongkan's wife, being of the same surname as Ge, wished to preserve him. She told Chengyan's mother, "Warn your son not to avenge others' grudges—one day the blame will be placed on you."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongkan's wife, sharing Ge's surname, wanted to protect him. She told Chengyan's mother: "Warn your son not to settle others' scores—the blame will fall on you one day.

sentences.zh: 承郾從之。

translations.literal: Chengyan followed her advice.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyan took her advice.

sentences.zh: 凝績怒，因公事抵承郾罪。

translations.literal: Ningji grew angry and, on a matter of official business, charged Chengyan with a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Ningji grew angry and used an official pretext to charge Chengyan with a crime.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬申朔，蜀主以兼中書令王宗弼為巨鹿王，宗瑤為臨淄王，宗綰為臨洮王，宗播為臨穎王，宗裔、宗夔及兼侍中宗黯皆為琅邪郡王。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the first day renshen, the ruler of Shu enfeoffed Wang Zongbi, who also held the post of Director of the Secretariat, as Prince of Julu; Zongyao as Prince of Linzi; Zongwan as Prince of Lintao; Zongbo as Prince of Linying; and Zongyi, Zongkui, and Zongan, who also held the post of Palace Attendant, all as Princes of Langye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, renshen, the Shu ruler enfeoffed Wang Zongbi as Prince of Julu; Zongyao as Prince of Linzi; Zongwan as Prince of Lintao; Zongbo as Prince of Linying; and Zongyi, Zongkui, and Zongan as Princes of Langye.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以王宗侃為樂安王。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, Wang Zongkan was made Prince of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Wang Zongkan was made Prince of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以兵部尚書庾傳素為太子少保兼中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Yu Chunsu, Minister of War, was made Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince, concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Yu Chunsu, Minister of War, was made Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Co-Director.

sentences.zh: 蜀主不親政事，內外遷除皆出於王宗弼。

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu did not personally attend to government affairs; all appointments within and without came from Wang Zongbi.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler did not govern in person; all appointments came from Wang Zongbi.

sentences.zh: 宗弼納賄多私，上下咨怨。

translations.literal: Zongbi accepted bribes and pursued private gain, and resentment spread above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi took bribes and pursued private gain, and resentment spread through the court.

sentences.zh: 宋光嗣通敏善希合，蜀主寵任之，蜀由是遂衰。

translations.literal: Song Guangsi was quick-witted and skilled at pleasing others. The ruler of Shu favored and trusted him, and from this Shu began to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Song Guangsi was clever and skilled at flattery. The Shu ruler favored him, and from then on Shu began to decline.

sentences.zh: 吳徐溫入朝於廣陵，疑諸將皆預朱瑾之謀，欲大行誅戮。

translations.literal: Xu Wen of Wu came to court at Guangling, suspected that all the generals had taken part in Zhu Jin's plot, and wished to carry out widespread executions.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen of Wu came to court at Guangling, suspected all the generals of joining Zhu Jin's plot, and wanted a general purge.

sentences.zh: 徐知誥、嚴可求具陳徐知訓過惡，所以致禍之由，溫怒稍解，乃命網瑾骨於雷塘而葬之，責知訓將佐不能匡救，皆抵罪；

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao and Yan Keqiu fully set forth Xu Zhixun's faults and excesses and the reasons he brought disaster on himself. Wen's anger eased somewhat. He then ordered Jin's bones gathered from Leitang and buried, blamed Zhixun's officers and aides for failing to restrain and save him, and punished them all;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao and Yan Keqiu fully described Xu Zhixun's crimes and how he brought disaster on himself. Wen's anger eased. He had Jin's bones recovered from Leitang and buried, punished Zhixun's officers for failing to restrain him, and punished them all;

sentences.zh: 獨刁彥能屢有諫書，溫賞之。

translations.literal: Only Diao Yanneng had repeatedly submitted remonstrances, and Wen rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Diao Yanneng, who had repeatedly remonstrated, was rewarded.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以知誥為淮南節度行軍副使、內外馬步都軍副使、通判府事，兼江州團練使。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Zhigao was made deputy expeditionary commander of Huainan Circuit, deputy overall commander of inner and outer cavalry and infantry, administrator of headquarters affairs, and concurrently regimental commissioner of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Zhigao was made deputy expeditionary commander of Huainan, deputy overall army commander, administrator of headquarters affairs, and regimental commissioner of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以徐知諫權潤州團練事。

translations.literal: Xu Zhijian was given provisional charge of regimental affairs at Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhijian was given provisional charge of Runzhou regimental affairs.

sentences.zh: 溫還鎮金陵，總吳朝大綱，自餘庶政，皆決於知誥。

translations.literal: Wen returned to garrison Jinling and held the overall framework of the Wu court; all remaining routine government was decided by Zhigao.
translations.idiomatic: Wen returned to Jinling and held the overall reins of Wu government; all routine affairs were decided by Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 知誥悉反知訓所為，事吳王盡恭，接士大夫以謙，御眾以寬，約身以儉。

translations.literal: Zhigao completely reversed everything Zhixun had done: he served the King of Wu with full respect, received scholars and officials with humility, governed the masses with leniency, and restrained himself with frugality.
