translations.idiomatic: Zhigao reversed everything Zhixun had done: he served the King of Wu with full respect, treated officials humbly, ruled the people leniently, and lived frugally.

sentences.zh: 以吳王之命，悉蠲天祐十三年以前逋稅，餘俟豐年乃輸之。

translations.literal: By the King of Wu's order, all tax arrears before the thirteenth year of Tianyou were entirely remitted; the remainder would be paid only after a bountiful harvest.
translations.idiomatic: By the king's order all tax arrears before Tianyou year 13 were remitted; the rest would be paid only in good harvest years.

sentences.zh: 求賢才，納規諫，除奸猾，杜請托。

translations.literal: He sought talented men, accepted remonstrance and advice, removed the crafty and corrupt, and blocked patronage requests.
translations.idiomatic: He sought talent, welcomed remonstrance, removed the corrupt, and blocked patronage.

sentences.zh: 於是士民翕然歸心，雖宿將悍夫無不悅服，以宋齊丘為謀主。

translations.literal: Thereupon scholars and commoners alike turned their hearts to him in unity; even old generals and fierce warriors were all pleased to submit. He took Song Qiqiu as his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners alike rallied to him; even old generals and fierce warriors submitted willingly. He took Song Qiqiu as chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 先是，吳有丁口錢，又計畝輸錢，錢重物輕，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wu had a head-tax and also assessed money per mu of land. Money was valued and goods were cheap, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wu had a head-tax and a land tax paid in cash. Cash was valued over goods, and the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 齊丘說知誥，以為「錢非耕桑所得，今使民輸錢，是教民棄本逐末也。

translations.literal: Qiqiu advised Zhigao, saying, "Money is not obtained from farming and sericulture. Now to make the people pay money is to teach them to abandon the root and pursue the branch.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu advised Zhigao: "Money does not come from farming and sericulture. Making people pay in cash teaches them to abandon the root and chase profit.

sentences.zh: 請蠲丁口錢；

translations.literal: I ask that the head-tax be remitted;
translations.idiomatic: Abolish the head-tax;

sentences.zh: 自餘稅悉輸谷帛，紬絹匹直千錢者當稅三十。」

translations.literal: let all remaining taxes be paid in grain and cloth; for silk and satin worth a thousand cash per bolt, thirty should be levied as tax."
translations.idiomatic: let all other taxes be paid in grain and cloth; tax silk worth a thousand cash per bolt at thirty."

sentences.zh: 或曰：「如此，縣官歲失錢億萬計。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "If it is like this, the government will lose tens of millions in cash each year."
translations.idiomatic: Someone objected: "That would cost the treasury tens of millions each year.

sentences.zh: 齊丘曰：「安有民富而國家貧者邪！」

translations.literal: Qiqiu said, "How can the people be rich while the state is poor!"
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu replied: "How can the people be rich while the state is poor!

sentences.zh: 知誥從之。

translations.literal: Zhigao followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao agreed.

sentences.zh: 由是江、淮間曠土盡辟，桑柘滿野，國以富強。

translations.literal: Because of this, idle land between the Yangzi and Huai was all opened, mulberry and ramie filled the fields, and the state grew rich and strong.
translations.idiomatic: Idle land along the Yangzi and Huai was opened, mulberry and ramie filled the fields, and the state grew rich and strong.

sentences.zh: 知誥欲進用齊丘而徐溫惡之，以為殿直、軍判官。

translations.literal: Zhigao wished to promote Qiqiu, but Xu Wen disliked him and made him a palace attendant and army aide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao wanted to promote Qiqiu, but Xu Wen disliked him and made him a palace attendant and army aide.

sentences.zh: 知誥每夜引齊丘於水亭屏語，常至夜分，或居高堂，悉去屏障，獨置大爐，相向坐，不言，以鐵箸畫灰為字，隨以匙滅去之，故其所謀，人莫得而知也。

translations.literal: Each night Zhigao would bring Qiqiu to a waterside pavilion for private talk, often until midnight. Sometimes, seated in a high hall with all screens removed and only a large brazier placed between them, they would sit facing each other without speaking, writing characters in the ashes with iron chopsticks and immediately rubbing them out with a spoon. Thus their plans could not be known by anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Each night Zhigao met Qiqiu at a waterside pavilion in private, often until midnight. Sometimes in a high hall with all screens removed they sat facing each other by a brazier, writing in the ashes with iron chopsticks and rubbing the words away at once. No one could learn their plans.

sentences.zh: 虔州險固，吳軍攻之，久不下，軍中大疫，王祺病，吳以鎮南節度使劉信為虔州行營招討使，未幾，祺卒。

translations.literal: Qianzhou was strong and secure. Wu troops attacked it but could not take it for a long time. A great plague broke out in the army, and Wang Qi fell ill. Wu made Liu Xin, military governor of Zhennan, commander for pacification of the Qianzhou expeditionary camp. Before long, Qi died.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhou was strong and secure. Wu troops besieged it for a long time without success. Plague broke out in the army and Wang Qi fell ill. Wu made Liu Xin, military governor of Zhennan, commander of the Qianzhou expedition. Qi soon died.

sentences.zh: 譚全播求救於吳越、閩、楚。

translations.literal: Tan Quanbo sought rescue from Wuyue, Min, and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Quanbo sought help from Wuyue, Min, and Chu.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐以統軍使傳球為西南面行營應援使，將兵二萬攻信州；

translations.literal: Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, made Chuanqiu, army commander, relief commander of the southwestern expeditionary camp and led twenty thousand troops to attack Xinzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, made Chuanqiu relief commander of the southwestern expedition and led twenty thousand troops against Xinzhou;

sentences.zh: 楚將張可求將萬人屯古亭，閩兵屯雩都以救之。

translations.literal: the Chu general Zhang Keqiu led ten thousand men and encamped at Guting; Min troops encamped at Yudu to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Chu general Zhang Keqiu encamped ten thousand men at Guting; Min troops encamped at Yudu to help.

sentences.zh: 信州兵才數百，逆戰，不利；

translations.literal: Xinzhou had only several hundred troops. They met the attack but fared poorly;
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhou had only a few hundred troops. They fought back but fared poorly;

sentences.zh: 吳越兵圍其城。

translations.literal: Wuyue troops besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyue troops besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 刺史周本，啟關張虛幕於門內，召僚佐登城樓作樂宴飲，飛矢雨集，安坐不動；

translations.literal: The prefect Zhou Ben opened the gate, hung empty curtains inside the gate, summoned his staff to the tower for music and a banquet. Arrows fell like rain, yet he sat unmoved;
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhou Ben opened the gate, hung empty curtains inside, and summoned his staff to the tower for music and wine. Arrows fell like rain, but he sat unmoved;

sentences.zh: 吳越疑有伏兵，中夜，解圍去。

translations.literal: Wuyue suspected an ambush and, in the middle of the night, lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyue suspected an ambush and withdrew in the middle of the night.

sentences.zh: 吳以前舒州刺史陳璋為東南面應援招討使，將兵侵蘇、湖，錢傳球自信州南屯汀州。

translations.literal: Wu made Chen Zhang, former prefect of Shuzhou, relief commander for pacification on the southeast front and led troops to raid Su and Hu. Qian Chuanqiu moved south from Xinzhou and encamped at Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu made former Shuzhou prefect Chen Zhang relief commander on the southeast front and raided Su and Hu. Qian Chuanqiu moved south from Xinzhou and encamped at Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王遣間使持帛書會兵於吳，吳人辭以虔州之難。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin sent a secret envoy with a silk letter to join forces with Wu. The Wu people declined, citing the difficulty at Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin sent a secret envoy with a letter proposing a joint campaign. Wu declined, citing the crisis at Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王謀大舉入寇，周德威將幽州步騎三萬，李存審將滄景步騎萬人，李嗣源將邢洺步騎萬人，王處直遣將將易定步騎萬人，及麟、勝、雲、蔚、新、武等州諸部落奚、契丹、室韋、吐谷渾，皆以兵會之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin planned a major invasion. Zhou Dewei led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry from Youzhou; Li Cunshen led ten thousand infantry and cavalry from Cang and Jing; Li Siyuan led ten thousand infantry and cavalry from Xing and Ming; Wang Chuzhi sent a general leading ten thousand infantry and cavalry from Yi and Ding; and the Xi, Khitan, Shiwei, and Tuyuhun tribes of the prefectures of Lin, Sheng, Yun, Yu, Xin, Wu, and others all joined with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin planned a major invasion. Zhou Dewei led thirty thousand foot and horse from Youzhou; Li Cunshen ten thousand from Cang and Jing; Li Siyuan ten thousand from Xing and Ming; Wang Chuzhi's general ten thousand from Yi and Ding; and Xi, Khitan, Shiwei, and Tuyuhun tribes from Lin, Sheng, Yun, Yu, Xin, Wu, and other prefectures all joined with troops.

sentences.zh: 八月，並河東、魏博之兵，大閱於魏州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, combining the armies of Hedong and Weibo, he held a grand review at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he combined the Hedong and Weibo armies and held a grand review at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀諸王皆領軍使，彭王宗鼎謂其昆弟曰：「親王典兵，禍亂之本。

translations.literal: All the princes of Shu held army commands. Prince Peng Zongding told his brothers, "When imperial princes command armies, that is the root of calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: All Shu princes held army commands. Prince Peng Zongding told his brothers: "When princes command armies, that is the root of disaster.

sentences.zh: 今主少臣強，讒間將興，繕甲訓士，非吾輩所宜為也。」

translations.literal: Now the ruler is young and the ministers are strong; slander and strife will arise. To drill armor and train troops is not what we ought to do."
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is young and the ministers are strong; slander and strife will come. Drilling troops is not for us."

sentences.zh: 因固辭軍使，蜀主許之，但營書捨、植松竹自娛而已。

translations.literal: He therefore firmly declined the army command. The ruler of Shu consented and allowed him only to build a study, plant pine and bamboo, and amuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the command. The Shu ruler agreed and let him build a study, plant pine and bamboo, and amuse himself.

sentences.zh: 泰寧節度使張萬進，輕險好亂。

translations.literal: Zhang Wanjin, military governor of Taining, was frivolous, reckless, and fond of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wanjin, military governor of Taining, was reckless and fond of trouble.

sentences.zh: 時嬖倖用事，多求賂於萬進，萬進聞晉兵將出，己酉，遣使附於晉，且求援。

translations.literal: At the time favored minions held power and often demanded bribes from Wanjin. Hearing that Jin troops were about to march out, on the day jiyou he sent envoys to attach himself to Jin and also requested aid.
translations.idiomatic: Favored minions held power and often demanded bribes from Wanjin. Hearing Jin troops were about to march, on jiyou he sent envoys to Jin seeking alliance and aid.

sentences.zh: 以亳州團練使劉鄩為兗州安撫制置使，將兵討之。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, regimental commissioner of Bozhou, was made pacification and disposition commissioner of Yanzhou and led troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, regimental commissioner of Bozhou, was made pacification commissioner of Yanzhou and led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 甲子，蜀順德皇后殂。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the Shunde Empress of Shu died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the Shunde Empress of Shu died.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，蜀主以內給事王廷紹、歐陽晃、李周輅、宋光葆、宋承蘊、田魯儔等為將軍及軍使，皆干預政事，驕縱貪暴，大為蜀患，周庠切諫，不聽。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, the ruler of Shu made the inner attendants Wang Tingshao, Ouyang Huang, Li Zhou'e, Song Guangbao, Song Chengyun, Tian Luchou, and others generals and army commissioners. All intervened in government affairs, were arrogant, unrestrained, greedy, and violent, and became a great affliction to Shu. Zhou Xiang remonstrated sharply but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the Shu ruler made inner attendants Wang Tingshao, Ouyang Huang, Li Zhou'e, Song Guangbao, Song Chengyun, and Tian Luchou generals and army commissioners. They meddled in government, were arrogant and brutal, and became a great scourge. Zhou Xiang remonstrated sharply but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 晃患所居之隘，夜，因風縱火，焚西鄰軍營數百間，明旦，召匠廣其居；

translations.literal: Huang disliked how cramped his residence was. At night he set fire with the wind and burned several hundred neighboring barracks to the west. The next morning he summoned craftsmen to enlarge his residence;
translations.idiomatic: Huang disliked his cramped quarters. At night he set a fire with the wind and burned hundreds of neighboring barracks. The next morning he summoned craftsmen to enlarge his residence;

sentences.zh: 蜀主亦不之問。

translations.literal: the ruler of Shu did not question him about it.
translations.idiomatic: the Shu ruler did not question him.

sentences.zh: 光葆，光嗣之從弟也。

translations.literal: Guangbao was Guangsi's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbao was Guangsi's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 晉王自魏州如楊劉，引兵略鄆、濮而還，循河而上，軍於麻家渡。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin went from Weizhou to Yangliu, led troops to raid Yun and Pu and returned, followed the river upstream, and encamped at Majiadu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin went from Weizhou to Yangliu, raided Yun and Pu, followed the river upstream, and encamped at Majiadu.

sentences.zh: 賀瑰、謝彥章將梁兵屯濮州北行台村，相持不戰。

translations.literal: He Gui and Xie Yanzhang led Liang troops and encamped at Xingtai Village north of Puzhou. The two sides faced each other without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He Gui and Xie Yanzhang led Liang troops to Xingtai Village north of Puzhou. The two sides faced each other without fighting.

sentences.zh: 晉王好自引輕騎迫敵營挑戰，危窘者數四，賴李紹榮力戰翼衛之，得免。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin liked to lead light cavalry himself to press the enemy camp and provoke battle. He was in peril four or five times and escaped only because Li Shaorong fought fiercely to flank and guard him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince liked to lead light cavalry himself to provoke the enemy. He was in peril several times and escaped only because Li Shaorong fought fiercely to protect him.

sentences.zh: 趙王鎔及王處直皆遣使致書曰：「元元之命繫於王，本朝中興繫於王，奈何自輕如此！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao, Rong, and Wang Chuzhi both sent envoys with letters saying, "The lives of the common people depend on Your Highness; the revival of the dynasty depends on Your Highness—how can you treat yourself so lightly!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong of Zhao and Wang Chuzhi both sent letters: "The people's lives depend on you; the dynasty's revival depends on you—how can you risk yourself so lightly!

sentences.zh: 王笑謂使者曰：「定天下者，非百戰何由得之！

translations.literal: The prince smiled and told the envoys, "He who settles the realm under Heaven—how can he obtain it without a hundred battles!
translations.idiomatic: The prince smiled and told the envoys: "How can one win the realm without a hundred battles!

sentences.zh: 安可但深居帷房以自肥乎！」

translations.literal: How can one merely dwell deep in curtained chambers and grow fat!"
translations.idiomatic: How can one just hide in curtained chambers and grow soft!"

sentences.zh: 一旦，王將出營，都營使李存審扣馬泣諫曰：「大王當為天下自重。

translations.literal: One day, as the prince was about to leave camp, the camp commander Li Cunshen seized his horse's bridle and wept as he remonstrated, saying, "Your Highness ought to value yourself for the sake of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: One day as the prince was leaving camp, camp commander Li Cunshen seized his bridle and wept: "Your Highness must value yourself for the realm's sake.

sentences.zh: 彼先登陷陳，將士之職也，存審輩宜為之，非大王之事也。」

translations.literal: To be first to ascend and break the enemy line is the duty of officers and soldiers—we of Cunshen's sort ought to do it; it is not Your Highness's affair."
translations.idiomatic: Leading the charge is the soldiers' duty—we should do that, not Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 王為之攬轡而還。

translations.literal: The prince pulled the reins and turned back on his account.
translations.idiomatic: The prince pulled the reins and turned back.

sentences.zh: 他日，伺存審不在，策馬急出，顧謂左右曰：「老子妨人戲！」

translations.literal: Another day, when Cunshen was absent, he spurred his horse out in haste and turned to his attendants, saying, "That old man spoils my sport!"
translations.idiomatic: Another day, when Cunshen was absent, he spurred out and told his attendants: "That old man spoils my fun!

sentences.zh: 王以數百騎抵梁營，謝彥章伏精甲五千於堤下；

translations.literal: The prince reached the Liang camp with several hundred horsemen. Xie Yanzhang had hidden five thousand elite armored troops beneath the embankment;
translations.idiomatic: He reached the Liang camp with several hundred horsemen. Xie Yanzhang had hidden five thousand elite armored troops beneath the embankment;

sentences.zh: 王引十餘騎度堤，伏兵發，圍王數十重，王力戰於中，後騎繼之者攻之於外，僅得出。

translations.literal: the prince led a little over ten horsemen across the embankment. The ambush sprang, surrounding the prince in dozens of rings. He fought fiercely at the center while the cavalry following attacked from outside, and he barely got out.
translations.idiomatic: the prince crossed the embankment with a dozen horsemen. The ambush sprang and surrounded him in rings. He fought at the center while followers attacked from outside, and he barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 會李存審救至，梁兵乃退，王始以存審之言為忠。

translations.literal: When Li Cunshen's rescue arrived, the Liang troops withdrew, and the prince then recognized Cunshen's words as loyal.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cunshen arrived, the Liang troops withdrew, and the prince then knew Cunshen had spoken truly.

sentences.zh: 吳劉信遣其將張宣等夜將兵三千襲楚將張可求於古亭，破之；

translations.literal: Liu Xin of Wu sent his generals Zhang Xuan and others by night with three thousand troops to raid Chu general Zhang Keqiu at Guting and defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin of Wu sent Zhang Xuan and others by night with three thousand troops to raid Chu general Zhang Keqiu at Guting and defeated him;

sentences.zh: 又遣梁詮等將兵擊吳越及閩兵，二國聞楚兵敗，俱引歸。

translations.literal: he also sent Liang Quan and others to strike the Wuyue and Min troops. When the two states heard that Chu troops had been defeated, both withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent Liang Quan and others against the Wuyue and Min forces. Hearing Chu had been defeated, both withdrew.

sentences.zh: 梅山蠻寇邵州，楚將樊須擊走之。

translations.literal: Meishan barbarians raided Shaozhou. The Chu general Fan Xu drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Meishan tribes raided Shaozhou. Chu general Fan Xu drove them off.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬午，蜀內樞密使宋光嗣以判六軍讓兼中書令王宗弼，蜀主許之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day renwu, Song Guangsi, Commissioner of the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs, yielded administration of the Six Armies to Wang Zongbi, who also held the post of Director of the Secretariat, and the ruler of Shu consented.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renwu, Commissioner Song Guangsi yielded command of the Six Armies to Wang Zongbi, and the Shu ruler agreed.

sentences.zh: 吳劉信晝夜急攻虔州，斬首數千級，不能克；

translations.literal: Liu Xin of Wu attacked Qianzhou day and night with urgency, beheading several thousand, but could not take it;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin of Wu attacked Qianzhou day and night, killing thousands, but could not take it;

sentences.zh: 使人說譚全播，取質納賂而還。

translations.literal: he sent men to persuade Tan Quanbo, took hostages and bribes, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: he sent men to persuade Tan Quanbo, took hostages and bribes, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 徐溫大怒，杖信使者。

translations.literal: Xu Wen was furious and had Xin's envoy beaten with rods.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen was furious and had Xin's envoy beaten.

sentences.zh: 信子英彥典親兵，溫授英彥兵三千，曰：「汝父居上游之地，將十倍之眾，不能下一城，是反也！

translations.literal: Xin's son Yingyan commanded the personal troops. Wen gave Yingyan three thousand men and said, "Your father holds the upper ground with ten times the force and cannot take one city—this is rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Xin's son Yingyan commanded the personal troops. Wen gave Yingyan three thousand men and said: "Your father holds the high ground with ten times the force and cannot take one city—that is rebellion!

sentences.zh: 汝可以此兵往，與父同反！」

translations.literal: You may take these troops and rebel with your father!"
translations.idiomatic: Take these troops and rebel with your father!"

sentences.zh: 又使升州牙內指揮使朱景瑜與之俱，曰：「全播守卒皆農夫，饑窘逾年，妻子在外，重圍既解，相賀而去，聞大兵再往，必皆逃遁，全播所守者空城耳，往必克之。」

translations.literal: He also sent Zhu Jingyu, commander of the Inner Guard at Shengzhou, to go with him, saying, "Quanbo's garrison troops are all farmers. They have been hungry and distressed for more than a year, and their wives and children are outside. Once the siege was lifted they congratulated one another and left. If they hear a great army is coming again, they will surely all flee. Quanbo will be holding an empty city—go and you will certainly take it."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Shengzhou Inner Guard commander Zhu Jingyu with him, saying: "Quanbo's garrison are farmers. They have been hungry for over a year, their families are outside, and once the siege lifted they left rejoicing. If they hear a great army is coming again, they will flee. Quanbo will hold an empty city—go and you will take it.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，壬申，蜀葬神武聖文孝德明惠皇帝於永陵，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: In winter, in the eleventh month, on the day renshen, Shu buried the Emperor Shenwu Shengwen Xiaode Minghui at Yongling. His temple name was Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on renshen of the eleventh month, Shu buried Emperor Shenwu Shengwen Xiaode Minghui at Yongling with the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 越主巖祀南郊，大赦，改國號曰漢。

translations.literal: The ruler of Yue, Yan, performed the southern suburban sacrifice, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the state name to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yue ruler Liu Yan performed the southern suburban rite, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the state name to Han.

sentences.zh: 劉信聞徐溫之言，大懼，引兵還擊虔州。

translations.literal: When Liu Xin heard Xu Wen's words, he was greatly afraid and led troops back to attack Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Xu Wen's words, Liu Xin was terrified and led troops back to attack Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 先鋒始至，虔兵皆潰，譚全播奔雩都，追執之。

translations.literal: When the vanguard first arrived, the Qian troops all collapsed. Tan Quanbo fled to Yudu and was pursued and captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the vanguard arrived, Qian's troops collapsed. Tan Quanbo fled to Yudu and was captured.

sentences.zh: 吳以全播為右威衛將軍，領百勝節度使。

translations.literal: Wu made Quanbo General of the Right Victorious Guard and military governor of Baisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu made Quanbo General of the Right Victorious Guard and military governor of Baisheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，吳越王鏐常自虔州入貢，至是道絕，始自海道出登、萊，抵大梁。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, had regularly sent tribute through Qianzhou. Now the route was cut off, and for the first time he sent tribute by sea through Deng and Lai to reach Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, had sent tribute through Qianzhou. Now that route was cut, and for the first time he sent tribute by sea through Deng and Lai to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 初，吳徐溫自以權重而位卑，說吳王曰：「今大王與諸將皆為節度使，雖有都統之名，不足相臨制；

translations.literal: Earlier, Xu Wen of Wu, considering himself powerful in authority but low in rank, said to the King of Wu, "Now Your Highness and all the generals are military governors. Though you have the title of overall commander, it is not enough to command and control them;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xu Wen of Wu, powerful but low in rank, told the King of Wu: "You and the generals are all military governors. Your title of overall commander is not enough to command them;

sentences.zh: 請建吳國，稱帝而治。」

translations.literal: I ask that the state of Wu be established and that you declare yourself emperor and govern."
translations.idiomatic: Establish the state of Wu and declare yourself emperor."

sentences.zh: 王不許。

translations.literal: The king did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The king refused.

sentences.zh: 嚴可求屢勸溫以次子知詢代徐知誥知吳政，知誥與駱知祥謀，出可求為楚州刺史。

translations.literal: Yan Keqiu repeatedly urged Wen to have his second son Zhixun replace Xu Zhigao in governing Wu affairs. Zhigao plotted with Luo Zhixiang and transferred Keqiu out as prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Keqiu repeatedly urged Wen to replace Xu Zhigao with his second son Zhixun. Zhigao plotted with Luo Zhixiang and transferred Keqiu out as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 可求既受命，至金陵，見溫，說之曰：「吾奉唐正朔，常以興復為辭。

translations.literal: Once Keqiu had received his appointment and reached Jinling, he saw Wen and said to him, "We observe the Tang calendar and always speak of restoring the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his appointment Keqiu reached Jinling and told Wen: "We observe the Tang calendar and always speak of restoring the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 今朱、李方爭，朱氏日衰，李氏日熾。

translations.literal: Now Zhu and Li are contending; the Zhu clan declines daily while the Li clan grows daily stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhu and Li are fighting; the Zhu clan declines daily while the Li clan grows stronger.

sentences.zh: 一旦李氏有天下，吾能北面為之臣乎？

translations.literal: If one day the Li clan holds the realm under Heaven, can we face north and serve them as subjects?
translations.idiomatic: If one day the Li clan wins the realm, can we bow north and serve them?

sentences.zh: 不若先建吳國以系民望。」

translations.literal: It would be better to establish the state of Wu first to hold the people's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: Better to establish Wu first and hold the people's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 溫大悅，復留可求參總庶政，使草具禮儀。

translations.literal: Wen was greatly pleased, kept Keqiu to take part in overall routine government, and had him draft the ritual protocols.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was delighted, kept Keqiu to help govern, and had him draft the ritual protocols.

sentences.zh: 知誥知可求不可去，乃以女妻其子續。

translations.literal: Zhigao knew Keqiu could not be removed and therefore gave his daughter in marriage to Keqiu's son Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Keqiu could not be removed, Zhigao married his daughter to Keqiu's son Xu.

sentences.zh: 晉王欲趣大梁，而梁軍扼其前，堅壁不戰百餘日。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin wished to press toward Daliang, but the Liang army blocked his front and held fast in their camps without fighting for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin wanted to press toward Daliang, but the Liang army blocked his path and held fast without fighting for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚子朔，晉王進兵，距梁軍十里而捨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day gengzi, the Prince of Jin advanced his army and encamped ten li from the Liang force.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day gengzi, the Prince of Jin advanced and encamped ten li from the Liang army.

sentences.zh: 初，北面行營招討使賀瑰善將步兵，排陳使謝彥章善將騎兵，瑰惡其與己齊名。

translations.literal: Earlier, He Gui, commander for pacification of the northern expeditionary camp, was skilled at commanding infantry, and Xie Yanzhang, battle-line commander, was skilled at commanding cavalry. Gui resented that Yanzhang shared equal fame with him.
translations.idiomatic: He Gui, northern pacification commander, was skilled with infantry; Xie Yanzhang, battle-line commander, with cavalry. Gui resented sharing equal fame with him.

sentences.zh: 一日，瑰與彥章治兵於野，瑰指一高地曰：「此可以立柵。」

translations.literal: One day Gui and Yanzhang drilled troops in the field. Gui pointed to a high ground and said, "A palisade can be set here."
translations.idiomatic: One day Gui and Yanzhang drilled troops in the field. Gui pointed to high ground and said: "A palisade can go here.

sentences.zh: 至是，晉軍適置柵於其上，瑰疑彥章與晉通謀。

translations.literal: By this time the Jin army had just placed a palisade on it, and Gui suspected Yanzhang of colluding with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Jin army had placed a palisade there, and Gui suspected Yanzhang of colluding with Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑰屢欲戰，謂彥章曰：「主上悉以國兵授吾二人，社稷是賴。

translations.literal: Gui repeatedly wanted to fight and said to Yanzhang, "Our lord has entrusted all the state's armies to us two—the altars of state depend on us.
translations.idiomatic: Gui repeatedly wanted to fight and told Yanzhang: "The emperor has entrusted all the state's armies to us—the realm depends on us.

sentences.zh: 今強寇壓吾門，而逗遛不戰，可乎！」

translations.literal: Now a formidable enemy presses our gate, yet we delay and do not fight—is this acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: A formidable enemy is at our gate, yet we delay and do not fight—is that acceptable!"

sentences.zh: 彥章曰：「強寇憑陵，利在速戰。

translations.literal: Yanzhang said, "The formidable enemy relies on aggression; the advantage lies in swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang replied: "The enemy relies on aggression; the advantage lies in swift battle.

sentences.zh: 今深溝高壘，據其津要，彼安敢深入！

translations.literal: Now we have deep moats and high ramparts and hold the strategic passes—how would they dare to penetrate deeply!
translations.idiomatic: We have deep moats and high ramparts and hold the strategic passes—how would they dare advance deeply!

sentences.zh: 若輕與之戰，萬一蹉跌，則大事去矣。」

translations.literal: If we lightly join battle and by any chance stumble, the great enterprise will be lost."
translations.idiomatic: If we fight lightly and stumble once, the great enterprise is lost."

sentences.zh: 瑰益疑之，密譖之於帝，與行營馬步都虞候曹州刺史朱珪謀，因享士，伏甲，殺彥章及濮州刺史孟審澄、別將侯溫裕，以謀叛聞。

translations.literal: Gui grew all the more suspicious and secretly slandered Yanzhang to the emperor. He plotted with Zhu Gui, chief adjutant of cavalry and infantry of the expeditionary camp and prefect of Caozhou, and at a feast for the officers hid armed men and killed Yanzhang, Meng Shencheng, prefect of Puzhou, and the detached commander Hou Wenyue, reporting it as a plot of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Gui grew more suspicious and secretly denounced Yanzhang to the emperor. With Zhu Gui, chief adjutant and prefect of Caozhou, he hid armed men at an officers' feast and killed Yanzhang, Puzhou prefect Meng Shencheng, and detached commander Hou Wenyue, reporting it as treason.

sentences.zh: 審澄、溫裕，亦騎將之良者也。

translations.literal: Shencheng and Wenyue were also fine cavalry commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Shencheng and Wenyue were also excellent cavalry commanders.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以朱珪為匡國留後，癸丑，又以為平盧節度使兼行營馬步副指揮使以賞之。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Zhu Gui was made acting governor of Kuangguo. On the day guichou he was further made military governor of Pinglu and concurrently deputy commander of cavalry and infantry of the expeditionary camp as a reward.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Zhu Gui was made acting governor of Kuangguo. On guichou he was further made military governor of Pinglu and deputy expeditionary commander as a reward.

sentences.zh: 晉王聞彥章死，喜曰：「彼將帥自相魚肉，亡無日矣。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin heard that Yanzhang was dead, he said with pleasure, "Their generals are devouring one another like fish and meat—their destruction is near.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin heard Yanzhang was dead, he said with pleasure: "Their generals are devouring one another—their end is near.

sentences.zh: 賀瑰殘虐，失士卒心，我若引軍直指其國都，彼安得堅壁不動！

translations.literal: He Gui is cruel and tyrannical and has lost the hearts of his soldiers. If I lead the army straight at their capital, how can they hold fast in their camps without moving!
translations.idiomatic: He Gui is brutal and has lost his soldiers' loyalty. If I march straight on their capital, how can they stay behind their walls!

sentences.zh: 幸而一與之戰，蔑不勝矣。」

translations.literal: If by good fortune we join them in one battle, we cannot fail to win."
translations.idiomatic: If we meet them in battle, we cannot fail to win."

sentences.zh: 王欲自將萬騎直趣大梁，周德威曰：「梁人雖屠上將，其軍尚全，輕行徼利，未見其福。」

translations.literal: The prince wished to lead ten thousand horsemen himself straight toward Daliang. Zhou Dewei said, "Though the Liang have killed a chief general, their army is still intact. To march lightly seeking quick gain—I see no blessing in it."
translations.idiomatic: The prince wanted to lead ten thousand horsemen straight to Daliang. Zhou Dewei said: "Though the Liang killed a chief general, their army is still intact. A light march for quick gain brings no blessing.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 戊午，下令軍中老弱悉歸魏州，起師趨汴。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, he ordered all the old and weak in the army to return to Weizhou and raised the army to march on Bian.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu he sent the old and weak back to Weizhou and marched on Bian.

sentences.zh: 庚申，毀營而進，眾號十萬。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, he destroyed the camps and advanced. The force was said to number one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he broke camp and advanced with a force said to number one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，蜀改明年元曰乾德。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Shu changed the next year's era name to Qiande.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Shu set the next year's era name to Qiande.

sentences.zh: 賀瑰聞晉王已西，亦棄營而踵之。

translations.literal: When He Gui heard the Prince of Jin had already gone west, he too abandoned his camps and followed in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the Prince of Jin had marched west, He Gui abandoned camp and pursued.

sentences.zh: 晉王發魏博白丁三萬從軍，以供營柵之役，所至，營柵立成。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin mobilized thirty thousand common laborers from Weibo to follow the army for building camps and palisades. Wherever they arrived, camps and palisades were erected at once.
translations.idiomatic: The prince mobilized thirty thousand laborers from Weibo to build camps and palisades. Wherever they went, fortifications sprang up at once.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，至胡柳陂。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, they reached Huluyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu they reached Huluyang.

sentences.zh: 癸亥旦，候者言梁兵自後至矣。

translations.literal: At dawn on the day guihai, scouts reported that Liang troops were approaching from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on guihai scouts reported Liang troops approaching from the rear.

sentences.zh: 周德威曰：「賊倍道而來，未有所捨，我營柵已固，守備有餘，既深入敵境，動須萬全，不可輕發。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei said, "The enemy has come by forced march and has nowhere to halt. Our camps and palisades are already secure and our defenses ample. Having penetrated deep into enemy territory, every move must be fully safe—we must not act lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei said: "The enemy has marched hard and has nowhere to stop. Our camps are secure and our defenses ample. Deep in enemy territory, every move must be safe—we must not act rashly.

sentences.zh: 此去大梁至近，梁兵各念其家，內懷憤激，不以方略制之，恐難得志。

translations.literal: From here to Daliang is very close. The Liang soldiers each think of their homes and burn with anger within. If we do not control them by strategy, I fear it will be hard to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang is very close. The Liang soldiers think of home and burn with anger. Without strategy we may not succeed.

sentences.zh: 王宜按兵勿戰，德威請以騎兵擾之，使彼不得休息，至暮營壘未立，樵爨未具，乘其疲乏，可一舉滅也。」

translations.literal: Your Highness ought to hold the army and not fight. Dewei asks to harass them with cavalry so they cannot rest. By evening their camps will not be set, firewood and cooking not ready. Seizing their exhaustion, we can destroy them in one stroke."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness should hold the army and not fight. Let me harass them with cavalry so they cannot rest. By evening their camps won't be set and firewood won't be gathered. Seizing their exhaustion, we can destroy them at one stroke."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「前在河上恨不見賊，今賊至不擊，尚復何待，公何怯也！」

translations.literal: The prince said, "Before on the river I regretted not seeing the enemy. Now the enemy has come and we do not strike—what are we waiting for? How timid you are!"
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "On the river I regretted not meeting the enemy. Now they are here and we do not strike—what are we waiting for? How timid you are!

sentences.zh: 顧李存審曰：「敕輜重先發，吾為爾殿後，破賊而去！」

translations.literal: He turned to Li Cunshen and said, "Order the baggage train to set out first. I will cover your rear, break the enemy, and go!"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Li Cunshen: "Send the baggage train ahead. I'll cover your rear, break the enemy, and go!

sentences.zh: 即以親軍先出。

translations.literal: He then led his personal troops out first.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his personal troops out first.

sentences.zh: 德威不得已，引幽州兵從之，謂其子曰：「吾無死所矣。」

translations.literal: Dewei, having no choice, led the Youzhou troops after him and said to his son, "I have no place left to die."
translations.idiomatic: Dewei, having no choice, led the Youzhou troops after him and told his son: "I have no place left to die.

sentences.zh: 賀瑰結陳而至，橫亙數十里。

translations.literal: He Gui drew up in battle formation and arrived, stretching across several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: He Gui drew up in battle formation stretching across miles.

sentences.zh: 王帥銀槍都陷其陳，沖蕩擊斬，往返十餘里。

translations.literal: The prince led the Silver Spear Guard in breaking the enemy formation, charging, cutting down, and returning back and forth for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: The prince led the Silver Spear Guard through the enemy line, charging and cutting down men back and forth for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 行營左廂馬軍都指揮使、鄭州防禦使王彥章軍先敗，西走趣濮陽。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang, commander of the left wing cavalry of the expeditionary camp and defender of Zhengzhou, was defeated first and fled west toward Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang, left-wing cavalry commander and defender of Zhengzhou, was defeated first and fled west toward Puyang.

sentences.zh: 晉輜重在陳西，望見梁旗幟，驚潰，入幽州陳，幽州兵亦擾亂，自相蹈藉；

translations.literal: The Jin baggage train was west of the formation. Seeing Liang banners, it panicked and collapsed, rushing into the Youzhou formation. The Youzhou troops also fell into disorder and trampled one another;
translations.idiomatic: The Jin baggage train west of the line saw Liang banners, panicked, and rushed into the Youzhou formation. Youzhou troops fell into disorder and trampled one another;

sentences.zh: 周德威不能制，父子皆戰死。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei could not control them, and father and son both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei could not control them, and father and son both died in battle.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度副使王緘與輜重俱行，亦死。

translations.literal: Wang Jian, deputy military governor of Weibo, was traveling with the baggage train and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, deputy military governor of Weibo, was with the baggage train and also died.

sentences.zh: 晉兵無復部伍。

translations.literal: The Jin troops no longer had formation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army lost all formation.

sentences.zh: 梁兵四集，勢甚盛。

translations.literal: Liang troops gathered from all sides, and their momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Liang troops gathered from all sides in overwhelming force.

sentences.zh: 晉王據高丘收散兵，至日中，軍復振。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin held a high mound and gathered the scattered troops. By midday the army had rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: The prince held a high mound and gathered scattered troops. By midday the army had rallied.

sentences.zh: 陂中有土山，賀瑰引兵據之。

translations.literal: In the marsh there was an earthen hill. He Gui led troops to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: In the marsh was an earthen hill. He Gui seized it.

sentences.zh: 晉王謂將士曰：「今日得此山者勝，吾與汝曹奪之。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin told the officers and soldiers, "Whoever holds this hill today wins. I will seize it with you."
translations.idiomatic: The prince told his officers and men: "Whoever holds this hill today wins. I will seize it with you.

sentences.zh: 即引騎兵先登，李從珂與銀槍大將王建及以步卒繼之，梁兵紛紛而下，遂奪其山。

translations.literal: He then led the cavalry up first. Li Congke, the Silver Spear Guard general Wang Jianji, and infantry followed. Liang troops came down in disarray, and they seized the hill.
translations.idiomatic: He led the cavalry up first. Li Congke, Silver Spear Guard general Wang Jianji, and the infantry followed. Liang troops fell back in disarray, and they took the hill.

sentences.zh: 日向晡，賀瑰陳於山西，晉兵望之有懼色。

translations.literal: As the sun approached the hour of shen, He Gui formed battle lines west of the hill. The Jin troops looked on them with fear.
translations.idiomatic: As afternoon approached, He Gui formed lines west of the hill. The Jin troops looked on them with fear.

sentences.zh: 諸將以為諸軍未盡集，不若斂兵還營，詰朝復戰。

translations.literal: The generals thought the armies had not all assembled and that it would be better to gather the troops and return to camp, fighting again at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The generals thought not all units had assembled and proposed gathering the troops and returning to camp to fight again at dawn.

sentences.zh: 天平節度使、東南面招討使閻寶曰：「王彥章騎兵已入濮陽，山下惟步卒，向晚皆有歸志，我乘高趣下擊之，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Yan Bao, military governor of Tianping and commander for pacification on the southeast front, said, "Wang Yanzhang's cavalry has already entered Puyang. Below the hill there are only infantry. Toward evening they all wish to return home. If we strike down from the heights, we are sure to break them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bao, military governor of Tianping and southeastern pacification commander, said: "Wang Yanzhang's cavalry is already in Puyang. Below the hill are only infantry, and toward evening they all want to go home. If we strike down from the heights, we will break them.

sentences.zh: 今王深入敵境，偏師不利，若復引退，必為所乘。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness has penetrated deep into enemy territory and a detached force has fared poorly. If we withdraw again, we will surely be pursued and overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has penetrated deep into enemy territory and a detached force has fared poorly. If we withdraw again, we will be pursued and overcome.

sentences.zh: 諸軍未集者聞梁再克，必不戰自潰。

translations.literal: Those armies not yet assembled, hearing that Liang has won again, will surely collapse without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Units not yet assembled, hearing Liang has won again, will collapse without fighting.

sentences.zh: 凡決勝料敵，惟觀情勢，情勢已得，斷在不疑。

translations.literal: In deciding victory and estimating the enemy, one looks only at the situation. Once the situation is grasped, the decision must be made without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: In deciding victory one looks only at the situation. Once the situation is clear, act without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 王之成敗，在此一戰；

translations.literal: Your Highness's success or failure hangs on this one battle;
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's fate hangs on this one battle;

sentences.zh: 若不決力取勝，縱收餘眾北歸，河朔非王有也。」

translations.literal: if you do not resolve to win by force, then even if you gather the remaining troops and return north, Hebei will no longer be yours."
translations.idiomatic: if you do not resolve to win by force, then even gathering the survivors and returning north, Hebei will no longer be yours."

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使李嗣昭曰：「賊無營壘，日晚思歸，但以精騎擾之，使不得夕食，俟其引退，追擊可破也。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao, military governor of Zhaoyi, said, "The enemy has no camps or ramparts. Toward evening they think of returning. Send elite cavalry to harass them so they cannot eat at dusk. Wait until they withdraw, then pursue and you can break them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao, military governor of Zhaoyi, said: "The enemy has no camp. Toward evening they want to go home. Harass them with elite cavalry so they cannot eat at dusk. Wait until they withdraw, then pursue and break them.

sentences.zh: 我若斂兵還營，彼歸整眾復來，勝負未可知也。」

translations.literal: If we gather the troops and return to camp, they will go back, regroup, and come again—the outcome cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: If we gather the troops and return to camp, they will regroup and come again—the outcome is uncertain."

sentences.zh: 王建及擐甲橫槊而進曰：「賊大將已遁，王之騎軍一無所失，今擊此疲乏之眾，如拉朽耳。

translations.literal: Wang Jianji, buckling on armor and spear held level, advanced and said, "The enemy's chief general has already fled. Your Highness's cavalry has lost nothing. Now to strike this exhausted force is like pulling rotten wood.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianji, armor buckled and spear level, advanced and said: "The enemy's chief general has fled. Your Highness's cavalry has lost nothing. Striking this exhausted force is like pulling rotten wood.

sentences.zh: 王但登山，觀臣為王破賊。」

translations.literal: Your Highness need only ascend the hill and watch your servant break the enemy for you."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness need only climb the hill and watch me break the enemy."

sentences.zh: 王愕然曰：「非公等言，吾幾誤計。」

translations.literal: The prince, startled, said, "Had it not been for your words, I would nearly have erred in my plan."
translations.idiomatic: The prince, startled, said: "Without your words I would nearly have erred.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭、建及以騎兵大呼陷陳，諸軍繼之，梁兵大敗。

translations.literal: Sizhao, Jianji, and others led the cavalry in shouting as they broke the enemy line. The other armies followed, and the Liang troops were routed.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao, Jianji, and others led the cavalry shouting into the enemy line. The other armies followed, and the Liang troops were routed.

sentences.zh: 元城令吳瓊、貴鄉令胡裝，各帥白丁萬人，於山下曳柴揚塵，鼓噪以助其勢。

translations.literal: Wu Qiong, magistrate of Yuancheng, and Hu Zhuang, magistrate of Guixiang, each led ten thousand common laborers below the hill, dragging brush to raise dust and shouting with drums to boost the momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qiong, magistrate of Yuancheng, and Hu Zhuang, magistrate of Guixiang, each led ten thousand laborers below the hill dragging brush to raise dust and shouting with drums to boost the attack.

sentences.zh: 梁兵自相騰藉，棄甲山積，死亡者幾三萬人。

translations.literal: Liang troops trampled one another. Abandoned armor piled like hills, and the dead numbered nearly thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Liang troops trampled one another. Abandoned armor piled like hills, and nearly thirty thousand died.

sentences.zh: 裝，證之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zhuang was the great-grandson of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang was the great-grandson of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 是日，兩軍所喪士卒各三之二，皆不能振。

translations.literal: That day each army lost two-thirds of its soldiers, and neither could recover its strength.
translations.idiomatic: That day each army lost two-thirds of its men, and neither could recover.

sentences.zh: 晉王還營，聞周德威父子死，哭之慟，曰：「喪吾良將，是吾罪也！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin returned to camp. Hearing that Zhou Dewei and his son had died, he wept bitterly and said, "I have lost my fine general—this is my fault!"
translations.idiomatic: The prince returned to camp. Hearing Zhou Dewei and his son had died, he wept bitterly: "I have lost my fine general—this is my fault!

sentences.zh: 以其子幽州中軍兵馬使光輔為嵐州刺史。

translations.literal: He made Dewei's son Guangfu, commander of the Youzhou central army cavalry and infantry, prefect of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He made Dewei's son Guangfu, Youzhou central army commander, prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源與李從珂相失，見晉軍撓敗，不知王所之，或曰：「王已北渡河矣。」

translations.literal: Li Siyuan and Li Congke lost one another. Seeing the Jin army routed, not knowing where the prince had gone, someone said, "Your Highness has already crossed the river north."
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan and Li Congke lost one another. Seeing the Jin army routed and not knowing where the prince had gone, someone said: "The prince has already crossed north over the river.

sentences.zh: 嗣源遂乘冰北渡，將之相州。

translations.literal: Siyuan then crossed north over the ice and was about to go to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan crossed north over the ice and was about to go to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是日，從珂從王奪山，晚戰皆有功。

translations.literal: That day Congke followed the prince in seizing the hill and had merit in the late battle.
translations.idiomatic: That day Congke followed the prince in seizing the hill and fought well in the late battle.

sentences.zh: 甲子，晉王進攻濮陽，拔之。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the Prince of Jin attacked Puyang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the prince attacked Puyang and took it.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源知晉軍之捷，復來見王於濮陽，王不悅，曰：「公以吾為死邪？

translations.literal: When Li Siyuan learned of the Jin army's victory, he came again to see the prince at Puyang. The prince was displeased and said, "Do you take me for dead?
translations.idiomatic: When Li Siyuan learned of the Jin victory, he came to see the prince at Puyang. The prince was displeased: "Do you take me for dead?

sentences.zh: 渡河安之！」

translations.literal: Why cross the river to find safety!"
translations.idiomatic: Why cross the river to safety!"

sentences.zh: 嗣源頓首謝罪。

translations.literal: Siyuan kowtowed to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan kowtowed to apologize.

sentences.zh: 王以從珂有功，但賜大鐘酒以罰之，然自是待嗣源稍薄。

translations.literal: The prince, because Congke had merit, punished him only by giving him a great bell of wine, but from this time treated Siyuan somewhat more coldly.
translations.idiomatic: Because Congke had merit, the prince punished him only with a great bell of wine, but from then on treated Siyuan somewhat more coldly.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹主之弟撒剌阿撥號北大王，謀作亂於其國。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khitan ruler's younger brother Salabuo, titled Prince of the Northern Great, plotted rebellion in their state.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khitan ruler's brother Salabuo, titled Northern Great King, plotted rebellion in their realm.

sentences.zh: 事覺，契丹主數之曰：「汝與吾如手足，而汝興此心，我若殺汝，則與汝何異！」

translations.literal: When the plot was discovered, the Khitan ruler rebuked him, saying, "You and I are like hands and feet, yet you harbored this intent. If I kill you, how am I different from you!"
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, the Khitan ruler rebuked him: "You and I are like hands and feet, yet you harbored this intent. If I kill you, how am I different from you!

sentences.zh: 乃囚之期年而釋之。

translations.literal: He then imprisoned him for a year and released him.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned him for a year and released him.

sentences.zh: 撒剌阿撥帥其眾奔晉，晉王厚遇之，養為假子，任為刺史；

translations.literal: Salabuo led his followers in flight to Jin. The Prince of Jin treated him generously, adopted him as a nominal son, and appointed him prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Salabuo fled to Jin with his followers. The prince treated him generously, adopted him as a nominal son, and made him prefect;

sentences.zh: 胡柳之戰，以其妻子來奔。

translations.literal: at the Battle of Huluyang his wife and children came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: at the Battle of Huluyang his wife and children joined him.

sentences.zh: 晉軍至德勝渡，王彥章敗卒有走至大梁者，曰：「晉人戰勝，將至矣。」

translations.literal: When the Jin army reached Desheng Ford, defeated soldiers of Wang Yanzhang who had fled to Daliang said, "The Jin have won the battle and are about to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army reached Desheng Ford, Wang Yanzhang's defeated soldiers who had fled to Daliang said: "The Jin have won and are coming.

sentences.zh: 頃之，晉兵有先至大梁問次捨者，京城大恐。

translations.literal: Before long Jin troops arrived first at Daliang asking where to lodge, and the capital was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jin scouts reached Daliang asking where to lodge, and the capital was terrified.

sentences.zh: 帝驅市人登城，又欲奔洛陽，遇夜而止。

translations.literal: The emperor drove townspeople up onto the walls and also wished to flee to Luoyang, but stopped when night came.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drove townspeople onto the walls and wanted to flee to Luoyang, but stopped when night came.

sentences.zh: 敗卒至者不滿千人，傷夷逃散，各歸鄉里，月餘僅能成軍。

translations.literal: The defeated troops who arrived numbered fewer than a thousand. Wounded and scattered, each returned to his home village, and only after more than a month could an army be formed again.
translations.idiomatic: Fewer than a thousand defeated troops arrived. Wounded and scattered, they returned home, and only after more than a month could an army be formed again.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，蜀主祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the day xinsi, the ruler of Shu performed the southern suburban sacrifice and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on xinsi of the first month, the Shu ruler performed the southern suburban rite and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 晉李存審於德勝南北夾河築兩城而守之。

translations.literal: Li Cunshen of Jin built two cities north and south of Desheng on either side of the river and garrisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunshen built two cities north and south of Desheng on either side of the river and garrisoned them.

sentences.zh: 晉王以存審代周德威為內外番漢馬步總管。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin made Cunshen replace Zhou Dewei as overall commander of inner and outer, barbarian and Han, cavalry and infantry.
translations.idiomatic: The prince made Cunshen replace Zhou Dewei as overall commander of all inner and outer, barbarian and Han, horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 晉王還魏州，遣李嗣昭權知幽州軍府事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin returned to Weizhou and sent Li Sizhao to administer Youzhou military headquarters affairs on a provisional basis.
translations.idiomatic: The prince returned to Weizhou and sent Li Sizhao to provisionally administer Youzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 漢主巖立越國夫人馬氏為皇后，殷之女也。

translations.literal: The ruler of Han, Yan, made Lady Ma of Yueguo empress. She was a daughter of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Yan made Lady Ma of Yue empress. She was Yin's daughter.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙戌，蜀北路行營都招討、武德節度使王宗播等自散關擊岐，渡渭水，破岐將孟鐵山。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day bingxu, Wang Zongbo and others, overall commanders for pacification of the northern expeditionary camp and military governors of Wude, attacked Qi from Sanguan, crossed the Wei River, and defeated the Qi general Meng Tieshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingxu, Wang Zongbo and others, northern overall commanders and military governors of Wude, attacked Qi from Sanguan, crossed the Wei River, and defeated Qi general Meng Tieshan.

sentences.zh: 會大雨而還，分兵戍興元、鳳州及威武城。

translations.literal: They met with heavy rain and returned, leaving troops to garrison Xingyuan, Fengzhou, and Weiwu City.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain forced them back. They left garrisons at Xingyuan, Fengzhou, and Weiwu City.

sentences.zh: 戊子，天雄節度使、同平章事王宗昱攻隴州，不克。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, Wang Zongyu, military governor of Tianxiong and Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs, attacked Longzhou but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Wang Zongyu, military governor of Tianxiong and Co-Director, attacked Longzhou but failed.

sentences.zh: 蜀主奢縱無度，日與太后、太妃游宴於貴臣之家，及游近郡名山，飲酒賦詩，所費不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu was extravagant and unrestrained without limit. Day after day he feasted and toured with the Empress Dowager and Grand Consort at the homes of noble ministers, and also toured famous mountains in nearby prefectures, drinking wine and composing poetry. The expense was beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler was extravagantly unrestrained. Day after day he feasted and toured with the Empress Dowager and Grand Consort at nobles' homes and nearby mountains, drinking and composing poetry at expense beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 仗內教坊使嚴旭強取士民女子內宮中，或得厚賂而免之，以是累遷至蓬州刺史。

translations.literal: Yan Xu, commissioner of the Inner Music Office, forcibly took commoners' daughters into the palace. Some escaped by paying heavy bribes, and through this he was repeatedly promoted until he reached prefect of Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xu, commissioner of the Inner Music Office, forcibly took commoners' daughters into the palace. Some escaped by paying heavy bribes, and through this he rose to prefect of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 太后、太妃各出教令賣刺史、令、錄等官，每一官闕，數人爭納賂，賂多者得之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager and Grand Consort each issued edicts selling the posts of prefect, magistrate, registrar, and other offices. For each vacancy several people competed in paying bribes, and whoever paid most obtained the post.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager and Grand Consort sold prefect, magistrate, and registrar posts by edict. For each vacancy several people competed in bribes, and the highest bidder won.

sentences.zh: 晉王自領盧龍節度使，以中門使李紹宏提舉軍府事，代李嗣昭。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin personally assumed the post of military governor of Lulong and made Li Shaohong, inner-gate commissioner, administrator of military headquarters affairs, replacing Li Siyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The prince personally took the post of military governor of Lulong and made inner-gate commissioner Li Shaohong administrator of military headquarters, replacing Li Siyuan.

sentences.zh: 昭宏，宦者也，本姓馬，晉王賜姓名，使與知嵐州事孟知祥俱為河東、魏博中門使。

translations.literal: Shaohong was a eunuch, originally surnamed Ma. The Prince of Jin bestowed the surname and given name and made him, together with Meng Zhixiang, who administered Lanzhou affairs, inner-gate commissioners for Hedong and Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohong was a eunuch originally surnamed Ma. The prince bestowed a surname and given name and made him, with Lanzhou administrator Meng Zhixiang, inner-gate commissioners for Hedong and Weibo.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥又薦教練使雁門郭崇韜能治劇，王以為中門副使。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang also recommended Guo Chongtao of Yanmen, training commissioner, as able to handle difficult affairs, and the prince made him deputy inner-gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang also recommended training commissioner Guo Chongtao of Yanmen as able to handle difficult affairs, and the prince made him deputy inner-gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 崇韜倜儻有智略，臨事敢決，王寵待日隆。

translations.literal: Chongtao was bold and free-spirited, with wisdom and strategy, daring and decisive in affairs. The prince favored and treated him with growing esteem day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao was bold and resourceful, daring and decisive. The prince favored him more each day.

sentences.zh: 先是，中門使吳珪、張虔厚相繼獲罪，及紹宏出幽州，知祥懼禍，稱疾辭位，王乃以知祥為河東馬步都虞候，自是崇韜專典機密。

translations.literal: Earlier, the inner-gate commissioners Wu Gui and Zhang Qianhou had successively been punished for crimes. When Shaohong went out to Youzhou, Zhixiang feared disaster, claimed illness, and resigned his post. The prince then made Zhixiang chief adjutant of Hedong cavalry and infantry, and from this time Chongtao alone managed secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier inner-gate commissioners Wu Gui and Zhang Qianhou had been punished in succession. When Shaohong went to Youzhou, Zhixiang feared disaster, feigned illness, and resigned. The prince made Zhixiang chief adjutant of Hedong horse and foot, and from then on Chongtao alone managed secret affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔吳越王鏐大舉討淮南。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, to launch a major campaign against Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, to launch a major campaign against Huainan.

sentences.zh: 鏐以節度副大使傳瓘為諸軍都指揮使，帥戰艦五百艘，自東洲擊吳。

translations.literal: Liu made Chuanjian, deputy military governor, overall commander of all armies and led five hundred warships from Dongzhou to attack Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu made Chuanjian, deputy military governor, overall army commander and led five hundred warships from Dongzhou against Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳遣舒州刺史彭彥章及裨將陳汾拒之。

translations.literal: Wu sent Peng Yanzhang, prefect of Shuzhou, and the subordinate general Chen Fen to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent Shuzhou prefect Peng Yanzhang and subordinate general Chen Fen to resist them.

sentences.zh: 吳徐溫帥將吏籓鎮請吳王稱帝，吳王不許。

translations.literal: Xu Wen of Wu led generals, officials, and military governors in requesting that the King of Wu declare himself emperor. The king of Wu did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen of Wu led generals, officials, and military governors in asking the King of Wu to declare himself emperor. The king refused.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊戌朔，即吳國王位。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day wuxu, he assumed the throne of the state of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the first day of the fourth month, wuxu, he assumed the throne of Wu.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元武義。

translations.literal: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the era name Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 建宗廟社稷，置百官，宮殿文物皆用天子禮。

translations.literal: He built ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain, established the hundred offices, and used imperial rites for palace halls and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: He built ancestral temples and state altars, established the bureaucracy, and used imperial rites for palace halls and regalia.

sentences.zh: 以金繼土，臘用丑。

translations.literal: Metal succeeded earth, and the twelfth month used the branch chou.
translations.idiomatic: Metal succeeded earth, and the twelfth month used the branch chou.

sentences.zh: 改謚武忠王曰孝武王，廟號太祖，威王曰景王，尊母為太妃；

translations.literal: He changed the posthumous title of Prince Wuzhong to Prince Xiaowu with the temple name Taizu, and Prince Wei to Prince Jing, and honored his mother as Grand Consort;
translations.idiomatic: He changed Prince Wuzhong's posthumous title to Prince Xiaowu with temple name Taizu, Prince Wei to Prince Jing, and honored his mother as Grand Consort;

sentences.zh: 以徐溫為大丞相、都督中外諸軍事、諸道都統、鎮海、寧國節度使、守太尉兼中書令、東海郡王，以徐知誥為左僕射、參政事兼知內外諸軍事，仍領江州團練使，以揚府左司馬王令謀為內樞密使，營田副使嚴可求為門下侍郎，鹽鐵判官駱知祥為中書侍郎，前中書舍人盧擇為吏部尚書兼太常卿，掌書記殷文圭為翰林學士，館驛巡宮游恭為知制誥，前駕部員外郎楊迢為給事中。

translations.literal: he made Xu Wen Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs at Home and Abroad, Overall Commander of All Circuits, military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo, Guardian Grand Master and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Donghai Commandery; made Xu Zhigao Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, participant in government affairs and concurrently administrator of inner and outer military affairs, still holding the post of regimental commissioner of Jiangzhou; made Wang Lingmou, Left Assistant Administrator of Yang Prefecture, Commissioner of the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs; made Yan Keqiu, deputy commissioner of military colonies, Vice Director of the Chancellery; made Luo Zhixiang, salt and iron commissioner, Vice Director of the Secretariat; made Lu Ze, former Secretariat Drafting Officer, Minister of Personnel and concurrently Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; made Yin Wengui, chief secretary, Hanlin Academician; made You Gong, touring inspector of post stations, Drafting Officer for Proclamations; and made Yang Tiao, former outer-office member of the Department of Transport, Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He made Xu Wen Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief, Overall Commander of All Circuits, military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo, Grand Master and Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Donghai; Xu Zhigao Left Vice Director, participant in government, and administrator of military affairs, still regimental commissioner of Jiangzhou; Wang Lingmou Commissioner of the Inner Bureau of Military Affairs; Yan Keqiu Vice Director of the Chancellery; Luo Zhixiang Vice Director of the Secretariat; Lu Ze Minister of Personnel and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Yin Wengui Hanlin Academician; You Gong Drafting Officer for Proclamations; and Yang Tiao Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 擇，醴泉人；

translations.literal: Ze was a man of Liquan;
translations.idiomatic: Ze was from Liquan;

sentences.zh: 迢，敬之之孫也。

translations.literal: Tiao was the grandson of Jingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao was Jingzhi's grandson.

sentences.zh: 錢傳瓘與彭彥章遇；

translations.literal: Qian Chuanjian encountered Peng Yanzhang;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chuanjian encountered Peng Yanzhang;

sentences.zh: 傳瓘命每船皆載灰、豆及沙，乙巳，戰於狼山江。

translations.literal: Chuanjian ordered every ship to carry ash, beans, and sand. On the day yisi they fought on the Langshan River.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanjian ordered every ship to carry ash, beans, and sand. On yisi they fought on the Langshan River.

sentences.zh: 吳船乘風而進，傳瓘引舟避之，既過，自後隨之。

translations.literal: Wu ships advanced with the wind. Chuanjian drew his boats aside to avoid them, and once they had passed, followed from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Wu ships advanced with the wind. Chuanjian drew aside, then followed from behind once they had passed.

sentences.zh: 吳回船與戰，傳瓘使順風揚灰，吳人不能開目；

translations.literal: Wu turned their ships to fight. Chuanjian had ash raised with the wind, and Wu men could not open their eyes;
translations.idiomatic: Wu turned to fight. Chuanjian had ash blown with the wind, and Wu men could not open their eyes;

sentences.zh: 及船舷相接，傳瓘使散沙於己船而散豆於吳船，豆為戰血所漬，吳人踐之皆僵仆。

translations.literal: when the gunwales met, Chuanjian had sand scattered on his own ships and beans scattered on Wu ships. The beans were soaked with battle blood, and Wu men who stepped on them all stiffened and fell.
translations.idiomatic: when the gunwales met, Chuanjian scattered sand on his ships and beans on Wu ships. The beans were soaked with blood, and Wu men who stepped on them slipped and fell.

sentences.zh: 傳瓘因縱火焚吳船，吳兵大敗。

translations.literal: Chuanjian then set fire and burned the Wu ships. The Wu army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanjian then set fire to the Wu ships. The Wu army was routed.

sentences.zh: 彥章戰甚力，兵盡，繼之以木，身被數十創，陳汾按兵不救；

translations.literal: Yanzhang fought very fiercely. When his troops were exhausted, he continued with wooden clubs. He received dozens of wounds, and Chen Fen held his troops back without rescuing him;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang fought fiercely. When his troops were exhausted he fought on with wooden clubs, took dozens of wounds, and Chen Fen held back without rescuing him;

sentences.zh: 彥章知不免，遂自殺。

translations.literal: Yanzhang knew he could not escape and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, Yanzhang killed himself.

sentences.zh: 傳瓘俘吳裨將七十人，斬首千餘級，焚戰艦四百艘。

translations.literal: Chuanjian captured seventy Wu subordinate generals, beheaded more than a thousand, and burned four hundred warships.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanjian captured seventy Wu subordinate generals, beheaded more than a thousand, and burned four hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 吳人誅汾，籍沒家貲，以其半賜彥章家，稟其妻子終身。

translations.literal: The Wu people executed Fen, confiscated his household property, gave half to Yanzhang's family, and provided rations to his wife and children for life.
translations.idiomatic: Wu executed Fen, confiscated his property, gave half to Yanzhang's family, and provided for his wife and children for life.

sentences.zh: 賀瑰攻德勝南城，百道俱進，以竹笮聯艨艟十餘艘，蒙以牛革，設睥睨、戰格如城狀，橫於河流，以斷晉之救兵，使不得渡。

translations.literal: He Gui attacked the southern city of Desheng from a hundred directions at once. He linked more than ten mengchong warships with bamboo cables, covered them with ox hide, set parapets and battle platforms like a city wall, and stretched them across the river to block Jin relief troops from crossing.
translations.idiomatic: He Gui attacked Desheng's southern city from every direction. He linked more than ten mengchong warships with bamboo cables, covered them with ox hide, set parapets and battle platforms like a wall, and stretched them across the river to block Jin relief troops.

sentences.zh: 晉王自引兵馳往救之，陳於北岸，不能進；

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin personally led troops in haste to rescue them and formed battle lines on the north bank but could not advance;
translations.idiomatic: The prince personally led troops to the rescue and formed lines on the north bank but could not advance;

sentences.zh: 遣善游者馬破龍入南城，見守將氏延賞，延賞言矢石將盡，陷在頃刻。

translations.literal: he sent the strong swimmer Ma Polong into the southern city to see the defending general Shi Yanshang. Yanshang said arrows and stones were nearly exhausted and the fall was imminent.
translations.idiomatic: he sent strong swimmer Ma Polong into the southern city to see defender Shi Yanshang, who said arrows and stones were nearly gone and the city would fall at any moment.

sentences.zh: 晉王積金帛於軍門，募能破艨□童者；

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin piled gold and silks at the camp gate and recruited anyone who could break the mengchong blockade;
translations.idiomatic: The prince piled gold and silks at the camp gate and offered a reward to anyone who could break the mengchong blockade;

sentences.zh: 眾莫知為計，親將李建及曰：「賀瑰悉眾而來，冀此一舉；

translations.literal: No one knew what to do. The prince's personal general Wang Jianji said, "He Gui has brought all his forces, hoping for success in this one move;
translations.idiomatic: No one knew what to do. Personal general Wang Jianji said: "He Gui has brought all his forces, hoping for success in this one move;

sentences.zh: 若我軍不渡，則彼為得計。

translations.literal: if our army does not cross, he will have achieved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: if our army does not cross, he wins.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，建及請以死決之。」

translations.literal: In today's matter, Jianji asks to settle it with his life."
translations.idiomatic: On today's matter, Jianji asks to settle it with his life."

sentences.zh: 乃選效節敢死士得三百人，被鎧操斧，帥之乘舟而進。

translations.literal: He then selected three hundred loyal dare-to-die warriors, armored them and gave them axes, and led them forward in boats.
translations.idiomatic: He selected three hundred loyal dare-to-die warriors, armored them with axes, and led them forward in boats.

sentences.zh: 將至艨□童，流矢雨集，建及使操斧者入艨艟間，斧其竹笮，又以木罌載薪，沃油然火，於上流縱之，隨以巨艦實甲士，鼓噪攻之。

translations.literal: As they neared the mengchong blockade, arrows fell like rain. Jianji had the axemen enter among the mengchong ships and chop the bamboo cables. He also loaded firewood in wooden jars, poured oil, set them afire, and released them upstream, then followed with great ships filled with armored troops shouting as they attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Near the mengchong blockade arrows fell like rain. Jianji sent axemen into the mengchong ships to chop the bamboo cables, loaded firewood in jars with oil and set them afire upstream, then followed with great ships full of armored troops shouting as they attacked.

sentences.zh: 艨艟既斷，隨流而下，梁兵焚溺者殆半，晉兵乃得渡。

translations.literal: Once the mengchong ships were cut loose, they drifted downstream. Nearly half the Liang troops were burned or drowned, and the Jin troops were at last able to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Once the mengchong ships were cut loose they drifted downstream. Nearly half the Liang troops were burned or drowned, and the Jin troops at last crossed.

sentences.zh: 瑰解圍走，晉兵追之，至濮州而還。

translations.literal: Gui lifted the siege and fled. Jin troops pursued him to Puzhou and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gui lifted the siege and fled. Jin troops pursued him to Puzhou and returned.

sentences.zh: 瑰退屯行台村。

translations.literal: Gui withdrew and encamped at Xingtai Village.
translations.idiomatic: Gui withdrew to Xingtai Village.

sentences.zh: 蜀主命天策府諸將無得擅離屯戍。

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu ordered the generals of the Celestial Strategy Office not to leave their garrisons without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler ordered Celestial Strategy Office generals not to leave their garrisons without authorization.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁卯朔，左散旗軍使王承諤、承勳、承會違命，蜀主皆原之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day dingmao, Wang Cheng'e, Chengxun, and Chenghui, commanders of the Left Scattered Banner Army, disobeyed orders, and the ruler of Shu pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day dingmao, Left Scattered Banner Army commanders Wang Cheng'e, Chengxun, and Chenghui disobeyed orders, and the Shu ruler pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 自是禁令不行。

translations.literal: From this time prohibitions were not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: From then on orders were not enforced.

sentences.zh: 楚人攻荊南，高季昌求救於吳，吳命鎮南節度使劉信等帥洪、吉、撫、信步兵自瀏陽趣潭州，武昌節度使李簡等帥水軍攻復州。

translations.literal: Chu attacked Jingnan. Gao Jichang sought rescue from Wu. Wu ordered Liu Xin and others, military governors of Zhennan, to lead infantry from Hong, Ji, Fu, and Xin from Liuyang toward Tanzhou, and Li Jian and others, military governors of Wuchang, to lead naval forces against Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chu attacked Jingnan. Gao Jichang sought help from Wu. Wu ordered Liu Xin and others to lead infantry from Hong, Ji, Fu, and Xin from Liuyang toward Tanzhou, and Li Jian and others to lead naval forces against Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 信等至潭州東境，楚兵釋荊南引歸。

translations.literal: When Xin and the others reached the eastern border of Tanzhou, Chu troops released Jingnan and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin and the others reached eastern Tanzhou, Chu troops released Jingnan and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 簡等入復州，執其知州鮑唐。

translations.literal: Jian and the others entered Fuzhou and seized its prefect Bao Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and the others entered Fuzhou and seized prefect Bao Tang.

sentences.zh: 六月，吳人敗吳越兵於沙山。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wu defeated Wuyue troops at Mount Sha.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Wu defeated Wuyue troops at Mount Sha.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，吳越王鏐遣錢傳瓘將兵三萬攻吳常州，徐溫帥諸將拒之，右雄武統軍陳璋以水軍下海門出其後。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, sent Qian Chuanjian with thirty thousand troops to attack Changzhou in Wu. Xu Wen led the generals to resist, and Chen Zhang, commander of the Right Victorious Army, took naval forces down to Haimen to strike from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, sent Qian Chuanjian with thirty thousand troops against Changzhou. Xu Wen led the generals to resist, and Chen Zhang took naval forces down to Haimen to strike from the rear.

sentences.zh: 壬申，戰於無錫。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, they fought at Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen they fought at Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 會溫病熱，不能治軍，吳越攻中軍，飛矢雨集，鎮海節度判官陳彥謙遷中軍旗鼓於左，取貌類溫者，擐甲冑，號令軍事，溫得少息。

translations.literal: Wen happened to be ill with fever and could not command the army. Wuyue attacked the center. Arrows fell like rain. Chen Yanqian, military governor's aide of Zhenhai, moved the center banners and drums to the left, found a man who resembled Wen, armored him, and issued military orders, allowing Wen a brief rest.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had a fever and could not command. Wuyue attacked the center as arrows fell like rain. Chen Yanqian, Zhenhai staff officer, moved the center banners left, found a Wen lookalike, armored him, and issued orders, giving Wen a brief rest.

sentences.zh: 俄頃，疾稍間，出拒之。

translations.literal: Before long his illness eased somewhat and he went out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his fever eased and he went out to resist.

sentences.zh: 時久旱草枯，吳人乘風縱火，吳越兵亂，遂大敗，殺其將何逢、吳建，斬首萬級。

translations.literal: The drought had lasted long and the grass was dry. Wu men set fires with the wind. Wuyue troops fell into disorder and were routed. Generals He Feng and Wu Jian were killed and more than ten thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: After a long drought the grass was dry. Wu men set fires with the wind. Wuyue troops fell into disorder and were routed. Generals He Feng and Wu Jian were killed and more than ten thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 傳瓘遁去，追至山南，覆敗之。

translations.literal: Chuanjian fled. They pursued him to the south of the mountain and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanjian fled. They pursued him south of the mountain and defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 陳璋敗吳越於香彎。

translations.literal: Chen Zhang defeated Wuyue at Xiangwan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhang defeated Wuyue at Xiangwan.

sentences.zh: 溫募生獲叛將陳紹者賞錢百萬，指揮使崔彥章獲之。

translations.literal: Wen offered a reward of a million cash for capturing the defecting general Chen Shao alive. Commander Cui Yanzhang captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen offered a million cash for capturing defector Chen Shao alive. Commander Cui Yanzhang captured him.

sentences.zh: 紹勇而多謀，溫復使之典兵。

translations.literal: Shao was brave and full of stratagems. Wen again had him command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was brave and shrewd. Wen again put him in command of troops.

sentences.zh: 初，錦衣之役，吳馬軍指揮曹筠叛奔吳越，徐溫赦其妻子，厚遇之，遣間使告之曰：「使汝不得志而去，吾之過也，汝無以妻子為念。」

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Jinyi campaign, Wu cavalry commander Cao Yun defected to Wuyue. Xu Wen pardoned his wife and children and treated them generously. He sent a secret messenger to tell him, "That you left because you could not achieve your aims is my fault. Do not worry about your wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Jinyi campaign, Wu cavalry commander Cao Yun defected to Wuyue. Xu Wen pardoned his family and treated them generously. He sent a secret messenger: "That you left because you could not achieve your aims is my fault. Do not worry about your wife and children.

sentences.zh: 及是役，筠復奔吳。

translations.literal: In this campaign Yun defected back to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Yun defected back to Wu.

sentences.zh: 溫自數昔日不用筠言者三，而不問筠去來之罪，歸其田宅，復其軍職，筠內愧而卒。

translations.literal: Wen himself counted three times how he had not taken Yun's advice in the past, yet did not punish Yun for leaving and returning. He restored his fields and residence and reinstated his military post. Yun died of inward shame.
translations.idiomatic: Wen counted three times how he had ignored Yun's advice, yet did not punish him for leaving and returning. He restored his lands and post. Yun died of shame.

sentences.zh: 知誥請帥步卒二千，易吳越旗幟鎧仗，躡敗卒而東，襲取蘇州。

translations.literal: Zhigao requested to lead two thousand infantry, change into Wuyue banners, flags, armor, and weapons, follow the defeated troops eastward, and seize Suzhou by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao asked to lead two thousand infantry in Wuyue banners and armor, follow the defeated troops east, and seize Suzhou by surprise.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「爾策固善；

translations.literal: Wen said, "Your plan is indeed good;
translations.idiomatic: Wen said: "Your plan is good;

sentences.zh: 然吾且求息兵，未暇如汝言也。」

translations.literal: but I am seeking to cease hostilities and have no leisure for what you say."
translations.idiomatic: but I am seeking peace and have no time for that now."

sentences.zh: 諸將皆以為：「吳越所恃者舟楫，今大旱，水道涸，此天亡之時也，宜盡步騎之勢，一舉滅之。」

translations.literal: The generals all said, "What Wuyue relies on is boats. Now there is great drought and the waterways are dry. This is the time Heaven will destroy them. We ought to use all our infantry and cavalry and destroy them in one stroke."
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said: "Wuyue relies on boats. Now drought has dried the waterways. Heaven is destroying them. We should use all our foot and horse and destroy them at one stroke.

sentences.zh: 溫歎曰：「天下離亂久矣，民困已甚，錢公亦未易可輕；
