translations.literal: Wen sighed and said, "The realm has been torn by disorder for long. The people are already deeply distressed, and Lord Qian is not easily to be taken lightly either;
translations.idiomatic: Wen sighed: "The realm has been torn by disorder for long. The people are deeply distressed, and Lord Qian is not to be taken lightly;

sentences.zh: 若連兵不解，方為諸君之憂。

translations.literal: if warfare continues without end, that will become your worry.
translations.idiomatic: if war continues without end, that will become your worry.

sentences.zh: 今戰勝以懼之，戢兵以懷之，使兩地之民各安其業，君臣高枕，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: Now to win the battle and thereby frighten them, to sheathe arms and thereby win their hearts, to let the people of both regions each secure their livelihoods, and for ruler and ministers to rest easy on high pillows—would that not be joy!
translations.idiomatic: Win the battle and frighten them, sheathe arms and win their hearts, let people on both sides live in peace, and let rulers and ministers rest easy—would that not be joy!

sentences.zh: 多殺何為！」

translations.literal: What is the use of more killing!"
translations.idiomatic: What is the use of more killing!"

sentences.zh: 遂引還。

translations.literal: He then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐見何逢馬，悲不自勝，故將士心附之。

translations.literal: When Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, saw He Feng's horse, he was overcome with grief. Therefore the old generals and soldiers attached their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Liu saw He Feng's horse, he was overcome with grief. The old officers and soldiers therefore rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 寵姬鄭氏父犯法當死，左右為之請，鏐曰：「豈可以一婦人亂我法。」

translations.literal: The father of his favored concubine Lady Zheng had violated the law and deserved death. Those around him pleaded for him. Liu said, "How can I let one woman overturn my law."
translations.idiomatic: The father of favored concubine Lady Zheng had violated the law and deserved death. Attendants pleaded for him. Liu said: "How can I let one woman overturn my law.

sentences.zh: 出其女而斬之。

translations.literal: He sent out her daughter and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent out her daughter and executed him.

sentences.zh: 鏐自少在軍中，夜未嘗寐，倦極則就圓木小枕，或枕大鈴，寐熟輒欹而寤，名曰：「警枕」。

translations.literal: From youth Liu had been in the army and never slept through the night. When utterly exhausted he would rest his head on a small round-wood pillow or a large bell. When he slept deeply he would tilt and wake. He called it the "Alarm Pillow."
translations.idiomatic: “From youth Liu had been in the army and never slept through the night. When exhausted he rested on a small round-wood pillow or a large bell; when he slept deeply he would tilt and wake. He called it the Alarm Pillow.”

sentences.zh: 置粉盤於臥內，有所記則書盤中，比老不倦。

translations.literal: He kept a powder tray in his sleeping quarters and wrote in the tray when he had something to record, and even in old age he did not weary of it.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a powder tray in his sleeping quarters and wrote notes in it, and even in old age he never tired of it.

sentences.zh: 或寢方酣，外有白事者，令侍女振紙即寤。

translations.literal: Sometimes when he was sleeping soundly and someone outside reported business, he had a maid shake paper and he would wake at once.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes when he slept soundly and someone reported business outside, he had a maid shake paper and woke at once.

sentences.zh: 時彈銅丸於樓牆之外，以警直更者。

translations.literal: He would shoot copper pellets outside the tower wall to alert the night watch.
translations.idiomatic: He shot copper pellets outside the tower wall to alert the night watch.

sentences.zh: 嘗微行，夜叩北城門，吏不肯啟關，曰：「雖大王來亦不可啟。」

translations.literal: Once he traveled incognito and knocked at the north city gate at night. The clerk refused to open the gate and said, "Even if it is the Great King, the gate cannot be opened."
translations.idiomatic: Once he traveled incognito and knocked at the north gate at night. The clerk refused to open it: "Even the king cannot enter now.

sentences.zh: 乃自他門入。

translations.literal: He then entered through another gate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered through another gate.

sentences.zh: 明日，召北門吏，厚賜之。

translations.literal: The next day he summoned the north gate clerk and rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned the north gate clerk and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，吳王立其弟濛為廬江郡公，溥為丹楊郡公，潯為新安郡公，澈為鄱陽郡公，子繼明為廬陵郡公。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, the King of Wu enfeoffed his brother Meng as Duke of Lujiang Commandery, Pu as Duke of Danyang Commandery, Xun as Duke of Xin'an Commandery, Che as Duke of Poyang Commandery, and his son Jiming as Duke of Luling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the King of Wu enfeoffed his brother Meng as Duke of Lujiang, Pu as Duke of Danyang, Xun as Duke of Xin'an, Che as Duke of Poyang, and his son Jiming as Duke of Luling.

sentences.zh: 晉王歸晉陽，以巡官馮道為掌書記。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin returned to Jinyang and made Feng Dao, touring officer, chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The prince returned to Jinyang and made touring officer Feng Dao chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 中門使郭崇韜以諸將陪食者眾，請省其數。

translations.literal: The inner-gate commissioner Guo Chongtao, noting that many generals attended the prince's meals, requested that their number be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-gate commissioner Guo Chongtao, noting many generals attended the prince's meals, asked to reduce their number.

sentences.zh: 王怒曰：「孤為效死者設食，亦不得專，可令軍中別擇河北帥，孤自歸太原。」

translations.literal: The prince angrily said, "I set out food for those who would die in my service, and I may not even decide that alone. Let the army choose another Hebei commander—I will return to Taiyuan myself."
translations.idiomatic: The prince angrily said: "I set out food for those who would die for me, and I may not even decide that alone. Let the army choose another Hebei commander—I will return to Taiyuan myself.

sentences.zh: 即召馮道令草詞以示眾。

translations.literal: He immediately summoned Feng Dao and ordered him to draft a proclamation to show the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Feng Dao and ordered him to draft a proclamation to show the assembly.

sentences.zh: 道執筆逡巡不為，曰：「大王方平河南，定天下，崇韜所請未至大過；

translations.literal: Dao held the brush and hesitated without writing, saying, "Your Highness is just pacifying Henan and settling the realm under Heaven. What Chongtao requested is not too great an offense;
translations.idiomatic: Dao hesitated with brush in hand and said: "Your Highness is just pacifying Henan and settling the realm. What Chongtao requested is not too great an offense;

sentences.zh: 大王不從可矣，何必以此驚動遠近，使敵國聞之，謂大王君臣不和，非所以隆威望也。」

translations.literal: Your Highness may refuse if you wish—why must you alarm near and far with this, letting the enemy state hear and say that ruler and ministers are not in harmony? That is not the way to enhance authority."
translations.idiomatic: You may refuse if you wish—why alarm near and far and let the enemy hear that ruler and ministers are divided? That does not enhance authority."

sentences.zh: 會崇韜入謝，王乃止。

translations.literal: When Chongtao came in to apologize, the prince then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongtao came to apologize, the prince stopped.

sentences.zh: 初，唐滅高麗，天祐初，高麗石窟寺眇僧躬乂，聚眾據開州稱王，號大封國，至是，遣佐良尉金立奇入貢於吳。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tang destroyed Goryeo, in the early Tianyou era the blind monk Gongyi of Goryeo's Shiku Temple gathered a host, seized Kaizhou, and declared himself king under the title Great Feng State. By this time he sent Assistant Good Official Jin Liqi to pay tribute to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Tang destroyed Goryeo, in early Tianyou the blind monk Gongyi of Goryeo's Shiku Temple gathered followers, seized Kaizhou, and declared himself king of Great Feng. By this time he sent Jin Liqi to pay tribute to Wu.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙未朔，宣義節度使賀瑰卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day yimao, He Gui, military governor of Xuanyi, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the first day yimao, He Gui, military governor of Xuanyi, died.

sentences.zh: 以開封尹王瓚為北面行營招討使。

translations.literal: Wang Zan, Prefect of Kaifeng, was made commander for pacification of the northern expeditionary camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zan, Prefect of Kaifeng, was made northern pacification commander.

sentences.zh: 瓚將兵五萬，自黎陽渡河掩擊澶、魏，至頓丘，遇晉兵而旋，瓚為治嚴，令行禁止，據晉人上游十八里楊村，夾河築壘，運洛陽竹木造浮梁，自滑州饋運相繼。

translations.literal: Zan led fifty thousand troops, crossed the river from Liyang to strike secretly at Chan and Wei, reached Dunqiu, met Jin troops and turned back. Zan was strict in governance; orders were enforced without exception. He held Yangcun eighteen li upstream from the Jin position, built fortifications on both banks of the river, transported bamboo and timber from Luoyang to build a pontoon bridge, and had continuous supply convoys from Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zan led fifty thousand troops, crossed from Liyang to strike Chan and Wei, reached Dunqiu, met Jin troops and turned back. Strict in command, he held Yangcun eighteen li upstream, built fortifications on both banks, transported Luoyang timber for a pontoon bridge, and kept supplies flowing from Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 晉蕃漢馬步副總管、振武節度使李存進亦造浮梁於德勝，或曰：「浮梁須竹笮、鐵牛、石囷，我皆無之，何以能成！」

translations.literal: Li Cunjin, deputy overall commander of barbarian and Han cavalry and infantry and military governor of Zhenwu, also built a pontoon bridge at Desheng. Someone said, "A pontoon bridge requires bamboo cables, iron oxen, and stone bins—we have none of these. How can it be completed!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunjin, deputy overall commander and military governor of Zhenwu, also built a pontoon bridge at Desheng. Someone said: "A pontoon bridge needs bamboo cables, iron oxen, and stone bins—we have none. How can it be done!

sentences.zh: 存進不聽，以葦笮維巨艦，繫於土山巨木，逾月而成，人服其智。

translations.literal: Cunjin would not listen. He bound great ships with reed cables and tied them to huge trees on an earthen hill. In more than a month it was completed, and people admired his ingenuity.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjin refused to listen. He bound great ships with reed cables tied to huge trees on an earthen hill. In more than a month it was done, and people admired his ingenuity.

sentences.zh: 吳徐溫遣使以吳王書歸無錫之俘於吳越；

translations.literal: Xu Wen of Wu sent envoys with a letter from the King of Wu to return the captives from Wuxi to Wuyue;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen of Wu sent envoys with a letter from the King of Wu to return the Wuxi captives to Wuyue;

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐亦遣使請和於吳。

translations.literal: Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, also sent envoys requesting peace with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, also sent envoys requesting peace with Wu.

sentences.zh: 自是吳國休兵息民，三十餘州民樂業者二十餘年。

translations.literal: From this time Wu ceased hostilities and rested the people. In more than thirty prefectures the people lived in secure livelihoods for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wu ceased hostilities and rested the people. In more than thirty prefectures people lived in peace for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 吳王及徐溫屢遺吳越王鏐書，勸鏐自王其國；

translations.literal: The King of Wu and Xu Wen repeatedly sent letters to Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, urging Liu to declare himself king of his own state;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu and Xu Wen repeatedly urged Qian Liu to declare himself king of his own state;

sentences.zh: 鏐不從。

translations.literal: Liu did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Liu refused.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙寅，詔削劉巖官爵，命吳越王鏐討之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day bingyin, an edict stripped Liu Yan of rank and titles and ordered Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingyin, an edict stripped Liu Yan of rank and ordered Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 鏐雖受命，竟不行。

translations.literal: Though Liu accepted the order, in the end he did not march.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liu accepted the order, he never marched.

sentences.zh: 吳廬江公濛有材氣，常歎曰：「我國家而為它人所有，可乎！」

translations.literal: Meng, Duke of Lujiang in Wu, had talent and spirit. He often sighed and said, "Our state possessed by others—is that acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: Meng, Duke of Lujiang in Wu, was talented and spirited. He often sighed: "Our state possessed by others—is that acceptable!

sentences.zh: 徐溫聞而惡之。

translations.literal: When Xu Wen heard of it, he hated him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Wen heard of it, he hated him for it.
